1.1: In the beginning God made of nought heaven and earth.
1.2: Forsooth the earth was idle and void, and darknesses were on the face of depth; and the Spirit of the Lord was borne on the waters [[or the Spirit of God was borne upon the waters]].
1.3: And God said, Light be made, and the light was made.
1.4: And God saw the light, that it was good, and he parted the light from darknesses;
1.5: and he called the light, day, and the darknesses, night. And the eventide and the morrowtide was made, one day.
1.6: And God said, The firmament be made in the midst of waters, and part waters from waters.
1.7: And God made the firmament, and parted the waters that were under the firmament, from the waters that were on the firmament [[or that were above the firmament]]; and it was done so.
1.8: And God called the firmament, heaven. And the eventide and the morrowtide was made, the second day.
1.9: Forsooth God said, The waters, that be under heaven, be gathered into one place, and a dry place appear; and it was done so.
1.10: And God called the dry place, earth; and he called the gatherings together of waters, the seas. And God saw that it was good;
1.11: and said, The earth bring forth green herb, and making seed, and an apple tree making fruit by his kind, whose seed be in itself, on [[the]] earth; and it was done so.
1.12: And the earth brought forth green herb and making seed by his kind, and a tree making fruit, and each having seed by his kind. And God saw that it was good.
1.13: And the eventide and the morrowtide was made, the third day.
1.14: Forsooth God said, Lights be made in the firmament of heaven, and part they the day and night; and be they into signs, and times, and days, and years;
1.15: and shine those in the firmament of heaven, and lighten they the earth; and it was done so.
1.16: And God made two great lights, the greater light that it should be before to the day, and the lesser light that it should be before to the night; and God made stars;
1.17: and setted them in the firmament of heaven, that they should shine on [[the]] earth,
1.18: and that they should be before to the day and [[to the]] night, and should part light and darkness. And God saw that it was good.
1.19: And the eventide and the morrow-tide was made, the fourth day.
1.20: Also God said, The waters bring forth a reptile, either a creeping beast, of living soul, and a volatile, either a bird flying above [[the]] earth, under the firmament of heaven.
1.21: And God made of nought great whales, and each living soul and movable, which the waters have brought forth in their kinds; and God made of nought each volatile by his kind. And God saw that it was good;
1.22: and blessed them, and said, Wax ye, and be ye multiplied, and fill ye the waters of the sea, and [[the]] birds be multiplied on [[the]] earth.
1.23: And the eventide and the morrowtide was made, the fifth day.
1.24: And God said, The earth bring forth a living soul in his kind, work beasts, and reptiles, either creeping beasts, and unreasonable beasts of [[the]] earth, by their kinds; and it was done so.
1.25: And God made unreasonable beasts of the earth by their kinds, and work beasts, and each creeping beast of the earth in his kind. And God saw that it was good;
1.26: and said, Make we man to our image and likeness, and be he sovereign to the fishes of the sea, and to the volatiles of heaven, and to [[the]] unreasonable beasts of [[the]] earth, and to each creature, and to each creeping beast or each reptile, which is moved in [[the]] earth.
1.27: And God made of nought a man to his image and likeness; God made of nought a man, to the image of God; God made of nought them, male and female.
1.28: And God blessed them, and said, Increase ye, and be ye multiplied, and fill ye the earth, and make ye it subject; and be ye lords to the fishes of the sea, and to [[the]] volatiles of heaven, and to all living beasts that be moved on [[the]] earth.
1.29: And God said, Lo! I have given to you each herb bearing seed on [[the]] earth, and all trees that have in themselves the seed of their kind, that they be into meat to you;
1.30: and to all living beasts of [[the]] earth, and to each bird of heaven, and to all things that be moved in [[the]] earth, and in which is a living soul, that they have to eat; and it was done so.
1.31: And God saw all things which he made, and they were full good. And the eventide and the morrowtide was made, the sixth day.

2.1: Therefore heavens and earth be made perfect, and all the ornament of those [[or them]].
2.2: And God [[ful]] filled in the seventh day his work which he made; and he rested in the seventh day from all his work which he had made;
2.3: and he blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it; for in that day God ceased of all his work which he made of nought, that he should make.
2.4: These be the generations of heaven and of earth, in the day wherein the Lord God made heaven and earth,
2.5: and each little tree of [[the]] earth before that it sprang out in [[the]] earth; and he made each herb of the field before that it burgeoned. For the Lord God had not rained on the earth, and no man there was that wrought [[or might work]] the earth;
2.6: but a well went out of [[the]] earth, and moisted all the higher part of the earth.
2.7: Therefore the Lord God formed man of the slime of [[the]] earth, and breathed into his face the breathing of life; and man was made into a living soul.
2.8: Forsooth the Lord God planted at the beginning paradise of liking or the garden of Eden, wherein he set man whom he had formed.
2.9: And the Lord God brought forth of the earth each tree fair in sight, and sweet to eat; also he brought forth the tree of life in the midst of paradise, and the tree of knowing of good and of evil.
2.10: And a river went out from the place of liking or Eden to moist paradise or the garden, which river is parted from thence into four heads.
2.11: The name of the one river is Pishon, that it is that encompasseth all the land of Havilah, where gold cometh forth,
2.12: and the gold of that land is the best, and there is found bdellium, that is, a tree of spicery, and the stone onyx;
2.13: and the name of the second river is Gihon, that it is that encompasseth all the land of Ethiopia;
2.14: forsooth the name of the third river is Tigris, that goeth against Assyrians; soothly the fourth river is that Euphrates.
2.15: Therefore the Lord God took man, and set him in paradise of liking, that he should work and keep it.
2.16: And God commanded to him and said, Eat thou of each tree of paradise;
2.17: forsooth eat thou not of the tree of knowing of good and of evil; for in whatever day thou shalt eat thereof, thou shalt die by death.
2.18: And the Lord God said, It is not good that a man be alone; make we to him an helper like to himself.
2.19: And therefore when all living beasts of [[the]] earth, and all the volatiles of heaven, were formed of [[the]] earth, the Lord God brought those [[or them]] to Adam, that he should see what he should call those [[or them]]; for all thing that Adam called of living soul, that is the name thereof.
2.20: And Adam called by their names all living things, and all volatiles [[of heavens]], and all unreasonable beasts of [[the]] earth. Forsooth to Adam was not found an helper like him.
2.21: Therefore the Lord God sent sleep into Adam, and when he slept, God took one of his ribs, and filled flesh for it.
2.22: And the Lord God builded the rib which he had taken from Adam into a woman, and brought her to Adam.
2.23: And Adam said, This is now a bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; this shall be called virago, for she is taken of man.
2.24: Wherefore a man shall forsake [[his]] father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they shall be twain [[or two]] in one flesh.
2.25: Forsooth ever either was naked, that is, Adam and his wife, and they were not ashamed.

3.1: But the serpent was feller or more sly than all living beasts of [[the]] earth, which the Lord God had made. The which serpent said to the woman, Why commanded God to you, that ye should not eat of each tree of paradise?
3.2: To whom the woman answered, We eat of the fruit of trees that be in paradise;
3.3: soothly God commanded to us, that we should not eat of the fruit of the tree, which is in the midst of paradise, and that we should not touch it, lest peradventure we die.
3.4: Forsooth the serpent said to the woman, Ye shall not die by death;
3.5: for why God knoweth that in what-ever day ye shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil.
3.6: Therefore the woman saw that the tree was good, and sweet to eat, and fair to the eyes, and delightable in beholding; and she took of the fruit thereof, and ate, and gave to her husband, and he ate.
3.7: And the eyes of both were opened; and when they knew that they were naked, they sewed [[together]] the leaves of a fig tree, and made breeches to themselves.
3.8: And when they heard the voice of the Lord God going in paradise at the wind after midday, Adam and his wife hid them from the face of the Lord God in [[the]] midst of the trees of paradise.
3.9: And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him, Where art thou?
3.10: And Adam said, I heard thy voice in paradise, and I dreaded, for I was naked, and I hid me.
3.11: To whom the Lord said, Who showed to thee that thou were naked, no but for thou hast eaten of the tree of which I commanded to thee that thou shouldest not eat?
3.12: And Adam said, The woman which thou gavest for fellowship to me, gave me of the tree, and I ate.
3.13: And the Lord said to the woman, Why didest thou this thing? The which answered, The serpent deceived me, and I ate.
3.14: And the Lord God said to the serpent, For thou didest this, thou shalt be cursed among all [[the]] living things, and unreasonable beasts of [[the]] earth; thou shalt go on thy breast, and thou shalt eat earth in all the days of thy life.
3.15: I shall set [[or put]] enmities betwixt thee and the woman, and betwixt thy seed and her seed; she shall break thine head, and thou shalt set ambushes to her heel.
3.16: Also God said to the woman, I shall multiply thy wretchednesses and thy conceivings; in sorrow thou shalt bear thy children; and thou shalt be under power of thine husband, and he shall be lord of thee.
3.17: Soothly God said to Adam, For thou heardest the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded to thee that thou shouldest not eat, the earth shall be cursed in thy work, that is, for thy sin; in travails thou shalt eat thereof in all the days of thy life;
3.18: it shall bring forth thorns and briars to thee, and thou shalt eat herbs of the earth;
3.19: in [[the]] sweat of thy cheer, [[or face]], thou shalt eat thy bread, till thou turn again into the earth of which thou art taken; for thou art dust, and thou shalt turn again into dust.
3.20: And Adam called the name of his wife Eve, for she was the mother of all men living.
3.21: And the Lord God made coats of skins to Adam and Eve his wife, and clothed them;
3.22: and said, Lo! Adam is made as one of us, and knoweth good and evil; now therefore see ye, lest peradventure he put [[out]] his hand, and take [[also]] of the tree of life, and eat, and live without end.
3.23: And the Lord God sent him out of paradise of liking or the garden of Eden, that he should work the earth, of which he was taken.
3.24: And God casted out Adam, and setted before paradise of liking cherubim, that is, gave it unto the keeping of angels, and a sword of flame turning about to keep charge of the way of the tree of life.

4.1: Forsooth Adam knew Eve his wife, which conceived, and childed Cain, and said, I have gotten a man by God.
4.2: And again she childed his brother Abel. Forsooth Abel was a keeper of sheep, and Cain was an earth-tiller.
4.3: Soothly it was done after many days, that Cain offered gifts to the Lord of the fruits of the earth;
4.4: and Abel offered of the first engendered of his flock, and of the fatness of those [[or them]]. And the Lord beheld to Abel and to the gifts of him;
4.5: soothly he beheld not to Cain and to his gifts. And Cain was wroth greatly, and his cheer felled down.
4.6: And the Lord said to him, Why art thou wroth, and why felled down thy face?
4.7: Whether not if thou shalt do well, thou shalt receive well; but if thou doest evil, thy sin shall be present anon in the gates? but the desire thereof, that is, of sin, shall be under thee, and thou shalt be lord thereof.
4.8: And Cain said to Abel, his brother, Go we out. And when they were in the field, Cain rose against his brother Abel, and killed him.
4.9: And the Lord said to Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? Which answered, I know not; whether I am the keeper of my brother?
4.10: And God said to Cain, What hast thou done? the voice of the blood of thy brother crieth to me from [[the]] earth.
4.11: Now therefore thou shalt be cursed on [[the]] earth, that opened his mouth, and received of thine hand the blood of thy brother.
4.12: When thou shalt work the earth, it shall not give his fruits to thee; thou shalt be unstable of dwelling, and fleeing about on [[the]] earth, in all the days of thy life.
4.13: And Cain said to the Lord, My wickedness is more than that I deserve forgiveness;
4.14: lo! today thou castest me out from the face of the earth; and I shall be hid from thy face, and I shall be unstable of dwelling, and fleeing about in earth; therefore each man that shall find me shall slay me.
4.15: And the Lord said to him, It shall not be done so, but each man that shall slay Cain shall be punished sevenfold. And the Lord set a sign in Cain, that each man that should find him should not slay him.
4.16: And Cain went out from the face of the Lord, and dwelled fleeing about in [[the]] earth, at the east coast of Eden, that is, of earthly paradise.
4.17: Forsooth Cain knew his wife, which conceived, and childed Enoch; and Cain builded a city, and called the name thereof of the name of his son, Enoch.
4.18: Forsooth Enoch begat Irad; and Irad begat Mehujael; and Mehujael begat Methusael; and Methusael begat Lamech;
4.19: that took two wives, the name to the one wife was Adah, and the name to the other was Zillah.
4.20: And Adah begat Jabal, that was the father of dwellers in tents, and of shepherds;
4.21: and the name of his brother was Jubal; he was the father of the singers in harp and organ.
4.22: And Zillah begat Tubalcain, that was an hammer-beater, and [[a]] smith on all works of brass and of iron; forsooth the sister of Tubalcain was Naamah.
4.23: And Lamech said to his wives, Adah and Zillah, Ye wives of Lamech, hear my voice, and hearken to my words; for I have slain a man by my wounding, and a young waxing man by my violent beating;
4.24: vengeance shall be given seven-fold of Cain, forsooth of Lamech seventy times seven times.
4.25: Also yet Adam knew his wife, and she childed a son, and called his name Seth, and said, God hath put [[or set]] to me another seed for Abel, whom Cain killed.
4.26: But also a son was born to Seth, which son he called Enos; this began to call inwardly the name of the Lord.

5.1: This is the book of the generations of Adam, in the day wherein God made man of nought. God made man to the image and likeness of God;
5.2: God formed them male and female, and blessed them, and called the name of them Adam, in the day in which they were formed.
5.3: Forsooth Adam lived an hundred years and thirty, and begat a son to his image and likeness, and called his name Seth.
5.4: And the days of Adam after that he begat Seth were made eight hundred years, and he begat sons and daughters.
5.5: And all the time in which Adam lived was made nine hundred years and thirty, and he was dead.
5.6: And Seth lived an hundred and five years, and begat Enos.
5.7: And Seth lived after that he begat Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.8: And all the days of Seth were made nine hundred and twelve years, and he was dead.
5.9: Forsooth Enos lived ninety years, and begat Cainan;
5.10: after whose birth Enos lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.11: And all the days of Enos were made nine hundred and five years, and he was dead.
5.12: Also Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel.
5.13: And Cainan lived after that he begat Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.14: And all the days of Cainan were made nine hundred and ten years, and he was dead.
5.15: Forsooth Mahalaleel lived sixty years and five, and begat Jared.
5.16: And Mahalaleel lived after that he begat Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.17: And all the days of Mahalaleel were made eight hundred [[and]] ninety and five years, and he was dead.
5.18: And Jared lived an hundred and two and sixty years, and begat Enoch.
5.19: And Jared lived after that he begat Enoch eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.20: And all the days of Jared were made nine hundred and two and sixty years, and he was dead.
5.21: Forsooth Enoch lived five and sixty years, and begat Methuselah.
5.22: And Enoch went with God; and Enoch lived after that he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.23: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and five and sixty years.
5.24: And Enoch went with God, and appeared not afterward, for God took him away.
5.25: Also Methuselah lived an hundred and seven and eighty years, and begat Lamech.
5.26: And Methuselah lived after that he begat Lamech seven hundred and two and eighty years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.27: And all the days of Methuselah were made nine hundred and nine and sixty years, and he was dead.
5.28: Forsooth Lamech lived an hundred and two and eighty years, and begat a son;
5.29: and [[he]] called his name Noah, and said, This man shall comfort us of the works and travails of our hands, in the land which the Lord cursed.
5.30: And Lamech lived after that he begat Noah five hundred [[and]] ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters.
5.31: And all the days of Lamech were made seven hundred [[and]] seventy and seven years, and he was dead.
5.32: Forsooth Noah, when he was of five hundred years, begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

6.1: And when men began to be multiplied on [[the]] earth, and had begat daughters,
6.2: the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair, and took wives to them of all which they had chosen.
6.3: And God said, My spirit shall not dwell in man without end, for he is flesh; and the days of him shall be an hundred and twenty years.
6.4: Soothly giants were on the earth in those days, forsooth after that the sons of God entered [[in]] to the daughters of men, and those daughters begat; these were mighty of the world and famous men.
6.5: Soothly God saw that much malice of men was in [[the]] earth, and that all the thought of their heart was attentive, either given, to evil in all time,
6.6: and it repented him that he had made man in earth; and God was wary before against time to coming [[or to come]], and was touched with sorrow of heart within;
6.7: and said, I shall do away man, whom I made of nought, from the face of the earth; from man till to living things, from creeping beast till to the birds of heaven; for it repenteth me that I made them.
6.8: Forsooth Noah found grace before the Lord.
6.9: These be the generations of Noah. Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations; Noah went with God,
6.10: and begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
6.11: Forsooth the earth was corrupt before God, and was filled with wickedness.
6.12: And when God saw, that the earth was corrupt, for each flesh, or man, had corrupted his way on [[the]] earth,
6.13: he said to Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; the earth is filled with wickedness of the face of them, and I shall destroy them with the earth.
6.14: Make thou to thee a ship of wood hewn and planed; thou shalt make dwelling places in the ship, and thou shalt anoint it with pitch within and withoutforth.
6.15: And so thou shalt make it. The length of the ship shall be of three hundred cubits, the breadth shall be of fifty cubits, and the highness thereof shall be of thirty cubits.
6.16: Thou shalt make a window in the ship, and thou shalt end the highness thereof in a cubit; soothly thou shalt set the door of the ship in the side beneath; thou shalt make solars or upper rooms, and places of three chambers in the ship.
6.17: Lo! I shall bring waters of deluge, or great flood, on the earth, and I shall slay each flesh in which is the spirit of life under heaven, and all things that be in [[the]] earth, shall be wasted.
6.18: And I shall set my covenant of peace with thee; and thou shalt enter into the ship, [[thou]], and thy sons, and thy wife, and the wives of thy sons shall enter with thee.
6.19: And of all living beasts of all flesh, thou shalt bring into the ship twain [[or two]] and twain, of male kind and female, that they live with thee;
6.20: of birds by their kind, and of work beasts in their kind, and of each creeping beast of [[the]] earth, by their kind; twain [[or two]] and twain of all shall enter with thee, that they may live.
6.21: Therefore thou shalt take with thee of all meats that may be eaten, and thou shalt bear together at thee, and those shall be as well to thee as to the beasts into meat.
6.22: Therefore Noah did all things which God commanded to him.

7.1: Also the Lord said to Noah, Enter thou and all thine house into the ship, for I saw thee alone were just before me in this generation.
7.2: Of all clean living beasts, thou shalt take by seven and by seven, male and female; forsooth of unclean living beasts, thou shalt take by twain and by twain [[or two and two]], male and female;
7.3: and also of [[the]] volatiles [[or fowls]] of heaven, thou shalt take, by seven and by seven, male and female, that their seed be saved on the face of all earth.
7.4: For yet and after seven days, I shall rain on [[the]] earth forty days and forty nights, and I shall do away all substance which I made, from the face of [[the]] earth.
7.5: Therefore Noah did all things which the Lord commanded to him.
7.6: And he was of six hundred years, when the waters of the great flood flowed on [[the]] earth.
7.7: And Noah entered into the ship, and his sons, and his wife, and the wives of his sons, entered with him, for the waters of the great flood.
7.8: And of living beasts clean and unclean, and of [[the]] birds of heaven, and of each beast which is moved on [[the]] earth,
7.9: by twain and by twain [[or two and two]], male and female entered to Noah into the ship, as the Lord commanded to Noah.
7.10: And when seven days had passed, the waters of the great flood flowed on [[the]] earth.
7.11: In the six hundredth year of the life of Noah, in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, all the wells of the great sea were broken, and the windows of heaven were opened,
7.12: and rain was made on the earth forty days and forty nights.
7.13: In the end of that day Noah entered, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, his sons, and his wife, and the [[three]] wives of his sons, entered with them into the ship.
7.14: They entered, and each beast by his kind, and all work beasts in their kind, and each beast which is moved on [[the]] earth in his kind, and each volatile by his kind; all birds and all volatiles [[or fowls]],
7.15: entered to Noah into the ship, by twain and by twain [[or two and two]] of each flesh in which the spirit of life was.
7.16: And those that entered, entered male and female of each flesh, as God commanded to him. And the Lord enclosed him from withoutforth.
7.17: And the great flood was made forty days and forty nights on [[the]] earth, and the waters were multiplied, and raised the ship on high from the earth.
7.18: The waters flowed greatly, and filled all things in the face of the earth. Forsooth the ship was borne on the waters.
7.19: And the waters had mastery greatly on [[the]] earth, and all [[the]] high hills under all of heaven were covered;
7.20: the water was higher, by fifteen cubits, over the hills which it covered.
7.21: And each flesh was wasted that moved on [[the]] earth, of birds, of living beasts, of unreasonable beasts, and of all reptiles or all creeping beasts that creep on [[the]] earth.
7.22: All men, and all things in which the breathing of life was in [[the]] earth, were dead.
7.23: And God did away all the substance that was on [[the]] earth, from man till to beast, as well a creeping beast, as the birds of heaven; and those [[or they]] were done away from [[the]] earth. Forsooth Noah dwelled alone, and they that were with him in the ship.
7.24: And the waters of the great flood over-went the earth an hundred and fifty days.

8.1: Forsooth the Lord had mind of Noah, and of all living beasts, and of all work beasts, that were with him in the ship; and [[he]] brought a wind on the earth. And [[the]] waters were decreased, or assuaged,
8.2: and the wells of the sea were closed, and the windows of heaven were closed, and rains of heaven were ceased.
8.3: And [[the]] waters turned again from off the earth, and went again, and began to be decreased, or assuaged, after an hundred and fifty days.
8.4: And the ship rested in the seventh month, in the seven and twentieth day of the month, on the hills [[or mounts]] of Armenia.
8.5: And soothly the waters went and decreased till to the tenth month, for in the tenth month, in the first day of the month, the tops of [[the]] hills appeared.
8.6: And when forty days had passed, Noah opened the window of the ship which he had made,
8.7: and sent out a crow, which went out, and turned not again till the waters were dried on [[the]] earth.
8.8: Also Noah sent out a culver after him, to see if the waters had ceased then on the face of the earth;
8.9: and when the culver found not where her foot should rest, she turned again to him into the ship, for the waters were on all [[the]] earth; and Noah held forth his hand, and brought the culver taken into the ship.
8.10: Soothly when other seven days were abided afterward, again he sent out a culver from the ship;
8.11: and she came to him at eventide, and bare in her mouth a branch of an olive tree with green leaves. There-fore Noah understood that the waters had ceased or abated on earth;
8.12: and nevertheless he abode seven other days, and sent out a culver, which turned not again to him.
8.13: Therefore in the six hundred and one year of the life of Noah, in the first month, in the first day of the month, [[the]] waters were decreased on earth; and Noah opened the roof of the ship, and beheld, and saw that the face of the earth was dried.
8.14: In the second month, in the seven and twentieth day of the month, the earth was made dry.
8.15: Soothly the Lord spake to Noah; and said,
8.16: Go out of the ship, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and the wives of thy sons with thee;
8.17: and lead out with thee all living beasts that be with thee of each flesh, as well in volatiles, as in unreason-able beasts, and all reptiles or all creeping beasts that creep on [[the]] earth; and enter ye on the earth, increase ye, and be ye multiplied on earth.
8.18: Therefore Noah went out, and his sons, and his wife, and the wives of his sons with him;
8.19: but also all living beasts, and work beasts, and birds, and reptiles that creep on [[the]] earth, by their kind, went out of the ship.
8.20: Forsooth Noah builded an altar to the Lord, and he took of all clean beasts and birds, and offered burnt sacrifices on the altar.
8.21: And the Lord savoured the odour of sweetness, and said to him, I shall no more curse the earth for men, for the wit and thought of man’s heart be ready, either prone, into evil from young waxing age; therefore I shall no more smite each living soul, as I did;
8.22: in all the days of [[the]] earth, seed and ripe corn, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day, shall not rest.

9.1: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, Increase ye, and be ye multiplied, and fill ye the earth;
9.2: and your dread and trembling be on all [[the]] unreasonable beasts of the earth, and on all [[the]] birds of heaven, with all things that be moved in earth; all fishes of the sea be given to your hand.
9.3: And all thing which is moved and liveth shall be to you into meat; I have given to you all things, as I gave the green worts before,
9.4: except that ye shall not eat flesh with the blood,
9.5: for I shall seek the blood of your lives, of the hand of all unreasonable beasts and of the hand of man, of the hand of man and of his brother, I shall seek the life of man.
9.6: Whoever sheddeth out man’s blood, his blood shall be shed; for man is made to the image of God.
9.7: Forsooth increase ye, and be ye multiplied, and enter ye on [[the]] earth, and fill ye it.
9.8: Also the Lord said these things to Noah, and to his sons with him,
9.9: Lo! I shall make my covenant with you, and with your seed after you,
9.10: and to each living soul which is with you, as well in birds as in work beasts and small beasts of [[the]] earth, and to all things that went out of the ship, and to all unreasonable beasts of [[the]] earth.
9.11: I shall make my covenant with you, and each flesh shall no more be slain of the waters of the great flood, neither the great flood destroying all [[the]] earth shall be any more.
9.12: And God said, This is the sign of bond of peace, which I give between me and you, and to each living soul which is with you, into everlasting generations.
9.13: I shall set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of bond of peace between me and [[the]] earth;
9.14: and when I shall cover [[the]] heaven with clouds, my bow shall appear in the clouds,
9.15: and I shall have mind of my bond of peace which I made with you, and with each soul living that nourisheth flesh; and the waters of the great flood shall no more be to do away all flesh.
9.16: And my bow shall be in the clouds, and I shall see it, and I shall have mind of the everlasting bond of peace, which is made between God and man, and each soul living of all flesh which is on [[the]] earth.
9.17: And God said to Noah, This shall be a sign of [[the]] bond of peace, which I made between me and each flesh on earth.
9.18: Therefore they that went out of the ship were Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth; forsooth Ham, that is the father of Canaan.
9.19: These three were the sons of Noah, and all the kind of men was sown of them on all [[the]] earth.
9.20: And Noah, an earth-tiller, began to till the earth, and he planted a vinery [[or a vineyard]],
9.21: and one day he drank wine, and was drunken; and he was naked, and lay in his tabernacle.
9.22: And when Ham, the father of Canaan, had seen this thing, that is, that the shameful members of his father were made naked, he told his two brethren withoutforth.
9.23: And Shem and Japheth putted a mantle on their shoulders, and they went backward, and covered the shameful members of their father, and their faces were turned away, and they saw not the privy members of their father.
9.24: And Noah waked of the wine, and when he had learned what things his lesser, or younger, son had done to him,
9.25: he said, Cursed be the child Canaan, he shall be a servant of servants to his brethren.
9.26: And Noah said, Blessed be the Lord God of Shem, and Canaan be the servant of Shem;
9.27: God alarge Japheth, and dwell he in the tabernacles of Shem, and Canaan be the servant of him.
9.28: Forsooth Noah lived after the great flood three hundred and fifty years;
9.29: and all the days of him were filled nine hundred and fifty years, and he was dead.

10.1: These be the generations of the sons of Noah; Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And sons were born to them after the great flood.
10.2: The sons of Japheth were Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
10.3: Forsooth the sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
10.4: Forsooth the sons of Javan were Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim;
10.5: of these sons the isles of the heathen men were parted in their countries, each by his language, and meines, in his nations.
10.6: Soothly the sons of Ham were Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
10.7: Forsooth the sons of Cush were Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtechah. The sons of Raamah were Sheba, and Dedan.
10.8: Forsooth Cush begat Nimrod; he began to be mighty in [[the]] earth,
10.9: and he was a strong hunter, or oppressor, of men before the Lord; of him a proverb went out, As Nimrod, a strong hunter before the Lord.
10.10: Soothly the beginning of his realm was Babylon, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
10.11: Asshur went out of that land, and builded Nineveh, and [[the]] streets of the city, and Calah,
10.12: and Resen betwixt Nineveh and Calah; this is a great city.
10.13: And soothly Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
10.14: and Pathrusim, and Casluhim; of which the Philistines and Caphtorim came forth.
10.15: Forsooth Canaan engendered Sidon, his first engendered son, Heth,
10.18: and Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites; and [[the]] peoples of Canaanites were sown abroad by these men.
10.19: And the terms of Canaan were made to men coming from Sidon to Gerar, till to Gaza, till thou enter into Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboiim, till to Lasha.
10.20: These were the sons of Ham, in their kindreds, and languages, and generations, and lands, and folks.
10.21: Also of Shem were born the fathers of all the sons of Eber, and Japheth was the more, or elder, brother of Shem [[or Shem was the more or elder brother of Japheth]].
10.22: The sons of Shem were Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
10.23: The sons of Aram were Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
10.24: And soothly Arphaxad begat Salah, of whom Eber was born.
10.25: And two sons were born to Eber, the name to the one son was Peleg, for the land was parted in his days; and the name of his brother was Joktan.
10.26: And that Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
10.27: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
10.29: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab; all these were the sons of Joktan.
10.30: And the habitation of them was made from Mesha, as men goeth till to Sephar, an hill of the east.
10.31: These be the sons of Shem, by kindreds, and languages, and countries, in their folks.
10.32: These be the meines of Noah, by their peoples, and nations; [[the]] folks [[or Gentiles]] in [[the]] earth were parted of these after the great flood.

11.1: Forsooth the land was of one language, and of the same speech [[or the same words]].
11.2: And when they went forth from the east, they found a field in the land of Shinar, and they dwelled therein.
11.3: And one said to his neighbour, Come ye, and make we tilestones, and bake we those [[or them]] with fire; and they had tile for stones, and pitch, either strong glue, for mortar;
11.4: and they said, Come ye, and make we to us a city and a tower, whose highness stretch till to heaven; and make we solemn our name, before that we be parted into all lands.
11.5: Forsooth the Lord came down to see the city, and the tower, which the sons of Adam builded.
11.6: And he said, Lo! the people is one, and one language is to all, and they have begun to make this; neither they shall cease of their thoughts, till they [[ful]] fill those [[or them]] in work;
11.7: therefore come ye, go we down, and shame [[or confound]] we there the tongue of them, that each man hear not the voice of his neighbour.
11.8: And so the Lord separated them from that place into all lands; and they ceased to build the city.
11.9: And therefore the name thereof was called Babel, for the language of all [[the]] earth was confounded there; and from thence the Lord scattered them on the face of all countries.
11.10: These be the generations of Shem. Shem was an hundred years when he begat Arphaxad, two years after the great flood.
11.11: And Shem lived after that he begat Arphaxad five hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.12: Forsooth Arphaxad lived five and thirty years, and begat Salah;
11.13: and Arphaxad lived after that he begat Salah three hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.14: And Salah lived thirty years, and begat Eber;
11.15: and Salah lived after that he begat Eber four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.16: Soothly Eber lived four and thirty years, and begat Peleg;
11.17: and Eber lived after that he begat Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.18: Also Peleg lived thirty years, and begat Reu;
11.19: and Peleg lived after that he begat Reu two hundred and nine years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.20: And Reu lived two and thirty years, and begat Serug;
11.21: and Reu lived after that he begat Serug two hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.22: Soothly Serug lived thirty years, and begat Nahor;
11.23: and Serug lived after that he begat Nahor two hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.24: Forsooth Nahor lived nine and twenty years, and begat Terah;
11.25: and Nahor lived after that he begat Terah an hundred and nineteen years, and begat sons and daughters.
11.26: And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
11.27: Soothly these be the generations of Terah. Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Forsooth Haran begat Lot;
11.28: and Haran died before Terah, his father, in the land of his nativity, in Ur of Chaldees.
11.29: Forsooth Abram and Nahor wedded wives; the name of the wife of Abram was Sarai, and the name of the wife of Nahor was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, father of Milcah, and father of Iscah.
11.30: Soothly Sarai was barren, and had no children.
11.31: And so Terah took Abram, his son, and Lot, the son of Haran, his son, and Sarai, his daughter-in-law, the wife of Abram, his son, and led them out of Ur of Chaldees, that they should go into the land of Canaan; and they came unto Haran, and dwelled there.
11.32: And the days of Terah were made two hundred years and five, and he was dead in Haran.

12.1: Forsooth the Lord said to Abram, Go thou out of thy land, and of thy kindred, and of the house of thy father, and come thou into the land which I shall show to thee;
12.2: and I shall make thee into a great folk, and I shall bless thee, and I shall magnify thy name, and thou shalt be blessed;
12.3: I shall bless them that bless thee, and I shall curse them that curse thee; and all kindreds of [[the]] earth shall be blessed in thee.
12.4: And so Abram went out, as the Lord commanded him, and Lot went with him. Abram was five and seventy years when he went out of Haran.
12.5: And he took Sarai, his wife, and Lot, the son of his brother, and all the substance which they had in possession, and the men which they had begotten in Haran; and they went out that they should go into the land of Canaan. And when they came into it,
12.6: Abram passed through the land till to the place of Shechem, and till to the noble valley. Forsooth Canaanite was then in the land.
12.7: Soothly the Lord appeared to Abram, and said to him, I shall give this land to thy seed. And Abram built there an altar to the Lord, that appeared to him.
12.8: And from thence he passed forth to the hill [[or the mount of]] Bethel, that was against the east, and setted there his tabernacle, having Bethel from the west, and Hai from the east. And he builded also there an altar to the Lord, and inwardly called his name.
12.9: And Abram went going, and going forth over to the south.
12.10: Soothly hunger was made in the land; and Abram went down into Egypt, to be a pilgrim there, for hunger had the mastery in the land.
12.11: And when he was nigh to enter into Egypt, he said to Sarai, his wife, I know that thou art a fair woman,
12.12: and that when Egyptians shall see thee, they shall say, It is his wife, and they shall slay me, and keep thee.
12.13: Therefore, I beseech thee, say that thou art my sister, that it be well to me for thee, and that my life live for the love of thee.
12.14: And so when Abram had entered into Egypt, Egyptians saw the woman, that she was full fair;
12.15: and the princes told to Pharaoh, and praised her with him; and the woman was taken up into the house of Pharaoh.
12.16: Forsooth they used well Abram for her; and sheep, and oxen, and asses, and servants, and servantesses, and she-asses, and camels were given to him.
12.17: Forsooth the Lord beat Pharaoh and his house with most vengeances for Sarai, the wife of Abram.
12.18: And Pharaoh called Abram, and said to him, What is it that thou hast done to me? why showedest thou not to me that she was thy wife?
12.19: for what cause saidest thou, that she was thy sister, that I should take her into wife to me? Now therefore lo! thy wife; take thou her, and go.
12.20: And Pharaoh commanded to men on Abram, and they led forth him, and his wife, and all things that he had.

13.1: Therefore Abram ascended from Egypt, he, and his wife, and all things that he had; and Lot went with him, to the south coast.
13.2: Forsooth he was full rich in possessions of silver, and of gold.
13.3: And he turned again by the way in which he came from the south into Bethel, till to the place, in which before he had set a tabernacle, betwixt Bethel and Hai,
13.4: in the place of the altar which he made before, and inwardly called there the name of the Lord.
13.5: But also flocks of sheep, and droves of oxen, and tabernacles were to Lot, that was with Abram;
13.6: and the land might not take them, that they should dwell together, for the cattle of them was much, and they might not dwell in common.
13.7: Wherefore also strife was made betwixt the keepers of [[the]] flocks of Abram and of Lot. Forsooth Canaanites and Perizzites dwelled in that land in that time.
13.8: Therefore Abram said to Lot, I beseech thee, that no strife be betwixt me and thee, and betwixt my shepherds and thy shepherds; for we be brethren.
13.9: Lo! all the land is before thee, I beseech, depart thou from me; if thou go to the left side, I shall hold the right side; if thou choose the right side, I shall go to the left side.
13.10: And so Lot raised [[up]] his eyes, and saw about all the country of Jordan, which was all-moisted, before that the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, as paradise of the Lord, and as Egypt, as men come into Zoar.
13.11: And Lot chose to him the country about Jordan, and departed from the east; and they were parted each from his brother.
13.12: Abram dwelled in the land of Canaan; soothly Lot dwelled in [[the]] towns about Jordan, and abode in Sodom.
13.13: Forsooth men of Sodom were full wicked, and sinners greatly before the Lord.
13.14: And the Lord said to Abram, after that Lot was parted from him, Raise [[up]] thine eyes forthright, and see from the place in which thou art now, to the north and south, to the east and west;
13.15: I shall give all the land which thou seest to thee, and to thy seed, till into without end.
13.16: And I shall make thy seed as the dust of the earth; if any man may number the dust of the earth, also he shall be able to number thy seed.
13.17: Therefore rise thou, and pass through the land in his length and breadth, for I shall give it to thee.
13.18: Therefore Abram, moving his tabernacle, came and dwelled beside the valley of Mamre, which is in Hebron; and he builded there an altar to the Lord.

14.1: Forsooth it was done in that time, that Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch, king of Ellasar, and Chedor-laomer, king of Elamites, and Tidal, king of folks,
14.2: began battle against Bera, king of Sodom, and against Birsha, king of Gomorrah, and against Shinab, king of Admah, and against Shemeber, king of Zeboiim, and against the king of Bela, that Bela is Zoar.
14.3: All these came together into the valley of wood, which is now the sea of salt.
14.4: For in twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they departed from him.
14.5: Therefore Chedorlaomer came in the fourteenth year, and [[the]] kings that were with him, and they smited Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, and Zuzims with them, and Emims in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
14.6: and Horites in the hills of Seir, till to the field places of Elparan, which is in wilderness.
14.7: And they turned again, and came till to the well of Mishpat; that is Kadesh. And they smited all the country of men of Amalek, and Amorites, that dwelled in Hazazontamar.
14.8: And the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, also and the king of Bela, which is Zoar, went out, and [[they]] dressed battle array against them in the valley of wood,
14.9: that is, against Chedorlaomer, king of Elamites, and Tidal, king of folks or of Goiim, and Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch, king of Ellasar; four kings against five.
14.10: Forsooth the valley of wood had many pits of pitch, either strong glue; and so the king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah turned their backs, and felled down there; and they that were left fled to the hills.
14.11: Soothly they took away all the chattel [[or substance]] of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all things that pertain[[ed]] to meat, and went away;
14.12: also and they took away Lot and his chattel [[or substance]], the son of the brother of Abram, which Lot dwelled in Sodom.
14.13: And, lo! one that escaped, told to Abram the Hebrew, that dwelled in the valley of Mamre of Amorites, [[the]] brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner; for these [[had]] made covenant of peace with Abram.
14.14: And when Abram had heard this thing, that is, Lot, the son of his brother, was taken, he numbered his born servants made ready, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them till to Dan.
14.15: And when his fellows were separated, he felled on them in the night, and smote them, and pursued them till to Hobah, and Phenice, which is at the left side of Damascus.
14.16: And he brought again all the chattel [[or substance]], and Lot, the son of his brother, with his chattel [[or substance]], also women, and the people.
14.17: Soothly the king of Sodom went out into the meeting of him, after that he turned again from [[the]] slaying of Chedorlaomer, and of the kings that were with him, in the valley of Shaveh, which is the valley of the king.
14.18: And soothly Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought forth bread and wine, for he was the priest of the highest God;
14.19: and he blessed Abram, and said, Blessed be Abram of [[the]] high God, that made heaven and earth of nought,
14.20: and blessed be [[the]] high God, by whom defending, thine enemies be betaken into thine hands. And Abram gave tithes of all things to him.
14.21: Forsooth the king of Sodom said to Abram, Give thou the men to me; take thou other things to thee.
14.22: And Abram answered to him, I raise [[up]] mine hand to the high Lord God, Lord of heaven and of earth,
14.23: that from the thread of [[the]] woof till to the lanyard of the hose, I shall not take anything of all things that be thine, lest thou say, I [[have]] made Abram rich;
14.24: except these things which the young men ate, and the parts of men that came with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; these men shall take their parts.

15.1: And so when these things were done, the word of the Lord was made to Abram by a vision, and said, Abram, do not thou dread, I am thy defender, and thy meed is full great.
15.2: And Abram said, Lord God, what shalt thou give to me? I shall go without free children, and this Damascus, son of Eliezer, the procurator of mine house, shall be mine heir.
15.3: And Abram added, Soothly thou hast not given seed to me, and, lo! my born servant shall be mine heir.
15.4: And anon the word of the Lord was made to him, and said, This shall not be thine heir, but thou shalt have him heir, that shall go out of thy womb.
15.5: And the Lord led out Abram, and said to him, Behold thou heaven, and number the stars, if thou mayest. And the Lord said to Abram, So thy seed shall be.
15.6: Abram believed to God, and it was reckoned to him to rightwiseness.
15.7: And God said to him, I am the Lord, that led thee out of Ur of Chaldees, that I should give this land to thee, and thou shouldest have it in possession.
15.8: And Abram said, Lord God, where-by shall I know that I shall wield it?
15.9: And the Lord answered, and said, Take thou to me a cow of three years, and a goat of three years, and a ram of three years, and a turtledove, and a culver.
15.10: Which took all these things, and parted those [[or them]] by the midst [[or the middle]], and setted [[or put]] ever either part each against other; but he parted not the birds.
15.11: And fowls came down on the carrions, and Abram drove them away.
15.12: And when the sun was gone down, dread felled on Abram, and a great hideousness and dark assailed him.
15.13: And it was said to him, Know thou a before-knowing, that thy seed shall be [[a]] pilgrim four hundred years in a land not his own, and they shall make them subject to servage, and they shall torment them;
15.14: nevertheless I shall deem the folk to whom they shall serve; and after these things they shall go out with great chattel [[or substance]].
15.15: Forsooth thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace, and shalt be buried in good [[eld]] age.
15.16: Soothly in the fourth generation they shall turn again hither, for the wickedness of [[the]] Amorites be not yet [[full-]]filled, till to present time.
15.17: Therefore when the sun was gone down, a dark mist was made, and a furnace smoking appeared, and a lamp of fire, and passed through those partings.
15.18: In that day the Lord made a covenant of peace with Abram, and said, I shall give to thy seed this land, from the river of Egypt till to the great river Euphrates;
15.19: the lands of the Kenites, and Kenizzites, and Kadmonites,
15.20: and Hittites, and Perizzites, and Rephaims,
15.21: and Amorites, and Canaanites, and Girgashites, and Jebusites.

16.1: Therefore Sarai, the wife of Abram, had not engendered [[to him]] free children; but she had a servantess of Egypt, Hagar by name,
16.2: and Sarai said to her husband, Lo! the Lord hath closed me, that I should not bear child; enter thou [[in]] to my servantess, if in hap I shall take children, namely of her. And when he assented to her praying,
16.3: she took Hagar the Egyptian, her servantess, after ten years after that they began to inhabit the land of Canaan, and she gave Hagar as [[a]] wife to her husband.
16.4: And Abram entered [[in]] to Hagar; and Hagar saw that she had conceived, and she despised her lady.
16.5: And Sarai said to Abram, Thou doest wickedly against me; I gave my servantess into thy bosom, which seeth that she [[hath]] conceived, and despiseth me; the Lord deem betwixt me and thee.
16.6: And Abram answered and said to her, Lo! thy servantess is in thine hand; use thou her as thee liketh. Therefore for Sarai tormented her, she fled away.
16.7: And when the angel of the Lord had found her beside a well of water in wilderness, which well is in the way of Shur in desert,
16.8: he said to her, From whence comest thou Hagar, the servantess of Sarai, and whither goest thou? Which answered, I flee from the face of Sarai, my lady.
16.9: And the angel of the Lord said to her, Turn thou again to thy lady, and be thou meeked under her hands.
16.10: And again he said, I multiplying shall multiply thy seed, and it shall not be numbered for multitude.
16.11: And afterward he said, Lo! thou hast conceived, and thou shalt bear a son, and thou shalt call his name Ishmael, for the Lord hath heard thy torment;
16.12: this shall be a wild man; his hand shall be against all men, and the hands of all men shall be against him; and he shall set his tabernacles even against all his brethren.
16.13: Forsooth Hagar called the name of the Lord that spake to her, Thou God that sawest me; for she said, Forsooth here I saw the hinder things of him that saw me.
16.14: Therefore she called that well, The well of him that liveth and seeth me; that well is betwixt Kadesh and Bered.
16.15: And Hagar childed a son to Abram, which called his name Ishmael.
16.16: Abram was eighty years and six, when Hagar childed Ishmael to him.

17.1: Forsooth after that Abram began to be of ninety years and nine, the Lord appeared to him, and said to him, I am Almighty God; go thou before me, and be thou perfect;
17.2: and I shall set my covenant of peace betwixt me and thee; and I shall multiply thee full greatly.
17.3: And Abram felled down low on his face. And God said to him,
17.4: I am, and my covenant of peace is with thee, and thou shalt be the father of many folks;
17.5: and thy name shall no more be called Abram, but thou shalt be called Abraham, for I have made thee [[the]] father of many folks;
17.6: and I shall make thee to wax full greatly, and I shall set thee in folks, and kings shall go out of thee;
17.7: and I shall make my covenant between me and thee, and between thy seed after thee, in their generations, by everlasting bond of peace, that I be thy God, and of thy seed after thee;
17.8: and I shall give to thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land of thy pilgrimage, all the land of Canaan, into everlasting possession, and I shall be the God of them.
17.9: God said again to Abraham, And therefore thou shalt keep my covenant, and thy seed after thee, in their generations.
17.10: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, betwixt me and you, and thy seed after thee; each male kind of you shall be circumcised,
17.11: and ye shall circumcise the flesh of your man’s rod, that it be into a sign of bond of peace betwixt me and you.
17.12: A young child of eight days shall be circumcised in you, all male kind in your generations, as well a born servant [[of your household]], as a servant bought, shall be circumcised,
17.13: and whoever is of your kindred, he shall be circumcised; and my covenant shall be in your flesh into everlasting bond of peace.
17.14: A man whose flesh of his rod shall not be circumcised, that man shall be done away from his people; for he made void my covenant.
17.15: Also God said to Abraham, Thou shalt not call Sarai, thy wife, Sarai, but Sarah;
17.16: and I shall bless her, and of her I shall give to thee a son, whom I shall bless, and he shall be into nations, and kings of peoples shall be born of him.
17.17: Abraham felled down on his face, and laughed in his heart, and said, Guessest thou, whether a child shall be born to a man of an hundred years, and Sarah of ninety years shall bear a child?
17.18: And he said to the Lord, I would that Ishmael might live before thee.
17.19: And the Lord said to Abraham, Sarah, thy wife, shall bear a son to thee, and thou shalt call his name Isaac, and I shall make my covenant with him into everlasting bond of peace, and to his seed after him;
17.20: also on Ishmael I have heard thee, lo! I shall bless him, and I shall increase him, and I shall multiply him greatly; he shall engender twelve dukes, and I shall make him into a great folk.
17.21: Forsooth I shall make my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah shall child to thee in this time in the tother year.
17.22: And when the word of the speaker with him was ended, God ascended from Abraham.
17.23: Forsooth Abraham took Ishmael, his son, and all the born servants of his house, and all which he had bought, all the males of all men of his house, and circumcised the flesh of their rods, anon in that day, as the Lord commanded to him.
17.24: Abraham was of ninety years and nine when he circumcised the flesh of his rod,
17.25: and Ishmael, his son, had filled thirteen years in the time of his circumcision.
17.26: Abraham was circumcised in the same day, and Ishmael his son,
17.27: and all the men of his house, as well born servants, as those bought and aliens, were circumcised together.

18.1: Forsooth in the valley of Mamre the Lord appeared to Abraham, sitting in the door of his tabernacle, in that heat of the day.
18.2: And when Abraham had raised up his eyes, three men appeared to him, and stood nigh [[to]] him. And when he had seen them, he ran from the door of his tabernacle into the meeting of them, and he worshipped on [[the]] earth,
18.3: and said, Lord, if I have found grace in thine eyes, pass thou not thy servant,
18.4: but I shall bring a little water, and your feet be washed, and rest ye under the tree;
18.5: and I shall set before you a morsel of bread, and your heart be comforted; afterward ye shall pass [[forth]]; for therefore be ye bowed aside to your servant. Which said, Do thou as thou hast spoken.
18.6: Abraham hasted into the tabernacle, to Sarah, and said to her, Haste thou, mix three half bushels of clean flour; and make thou loaves baken under ashes.
18.7: Forsooth he ran to the drove of beasts, and took thereof a calf most tender and best, and gave to a servant, which hasted, and seethed the calf;
18.8: and he took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had sodden, and set before them; forsooth Abraham stood beside them under the tree. And when they had eaten,
18.9: they said to him, Where is Sarah thy wife? He answered, Lo! she is in the tabernacle.
18.10: To whom the Lord said, I shall turn again, and I shall come to thee in this time, if I live; and Sarah, thy wife, shall have a son. When this was heard, Sarah laughed behind the door of the tabernacle.
18.11: Forsooth both were old, and of great age, and woman’s terms ceased to be made to Sarah.
18.12: And she laughed, saying privily, After that I waxed eld [[or old]], and my lord is eld [[or old]], shall I give diligence [[or busyness]] to lust?
18.13: Forsooth the Lord said to Abraham, Why laughed Sarah, thy wife, saying, Whether I an eld [[or old]] woman shall bear a child verily?
18.14: whether anything is hard to God? By the promise I shall turn again to thee in this same time, if I live; and Sarah shall have a son.
18.15: Sarah was afeared for dread, and denied, saying, I laughed not. Forsooth the Lord said, It is not so, but thou laughedest.
18.16: Therefore when the men had risen from thence, they dressed the eyes against Sodom; and Abraham went together, leading them forth.
18.17: And the Lord said, Whether I may cover from Abraham what things I shall do,
18.18: since he shall be into a great folk and most strong, and all nations of [[the]] earth shall be blessed in him?
18.19: For I know that Abraham shall command his children, and his house after him, that they keep the way of the Lord, and that they do rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] and doom, that the Lord bring for Abraham all things which he spake to Abraham.
18.20: And so the Lord said, The cry of men of Sodom and of men of Gomorrah is multiplied, and their sin is egregious greatly;
18.21: I shall come down, and see whether they have [[ful]] filled in work the cry that came to me, that I know whether it is not so.
18.22: And they turned them[[selves]] from thence, and went to Sodom. Abraham soothly stood yet before the Lord,
18.23: and nighed, and said, Whether thou shalt lose a just man [[or the rightwise]] with the wicked?
18.24: if fifty just [[or rightwise]] men be in the city, shall they perish altogether, and shalt thou not spare that place for fifty just [[or rightwise]] men, if they be therein?
18.25: Far be it from thee that thou do this thing, and slay the just [[or rightwise]] with the wicked, and that a just [[or rightwise]] man be made as a wicked man; this is not thine that deemest all [[the]] earth; thou shalt not make this doom.
18.26: And the Lord said to him, If I shall find in Sodom fifty just [[or rightwise]] men in the midst of the city, I shall forgive to all the place for them.
18.27: Abraham answered and said, For I began once, I shall speak to my Lord, since I am dust and ashes;
18.28: what if less than fifty just [[or rightwise]] men by five be, shalt thou do away all the city for five and forty? And the Lord said, I shall not do away, if I shall find five and forty there.
18.29: And again Abraham said to him, But if forty be there, what shalt thou do? The Lord said, I shall not smite for forty.
18.30: Abraham said, Lord, I beseech, take thou not into indignation, if I speak; what if thirty be found there? The Lord answered, I shall not do, if I shall find thirty there.
18.31: Abraham said, For I began once, I shall speak to my Lord; what if twenty be found there? The Lord said, I shall not slay for twenty.
18.32: Abraham said, Lord, I beseech, be thou not wroth, if I speak yet once more; what if ten be found there? The Lord said, I shall not do away for ten.
18.33: The Lord went forth, after that he [[had]] ceased to speak to Abraham, and Abraham turned again into his place.

19.1: And twain angels came to Sodom in the eventide, while Lot sat in the gates of the city. And when he had seen them, he rose, and went to meet them, and worshipped or honoured low to the earth,
19.2: and said, My lords, I beseech, bow ye [[down]] into the house of your servant, and dwell ye there; wash ye your feet, and in the morrowtide ye shall go into your way. Which said, Nay, but we shall dwell in the street.
19.3: He constrained them greatly, that they should turn in to him. And when they entered into his house, he made a feast, and baked therf bread, and they ate.
19.4: Forsooth before that they went to sleep, men of the city compassed his house, from a child till to an eld [[or old]] man, all the people together;
19.5: and they called Lot, and said to him, Where be the men that entered to thee tonight? bring them out hither, that we know them, that is, by lechery against kind.
19.6: And Lot went out to them behind the back, and closed the door,
19.7: and said, I beseech, do not ye, my brethren, do not ye do this evil.
19.8: I have two daughters, that knew not yet a man; I shall lead out them to you, and mis-use ye them as it pleaseth you, so that ye do none evil to these men, for they entered under the shadow of my roof.
19.9: And they said, Go thou from hence. And again they said, Thou enteredest [[in]] hither as a comeling; whether that thou shalt deem us? therefore we shall torment thee more than these. And they did violently to Lot full greatly. Then it was nigh that they would break the doors;
19.10: and lo! the men put forth their hands, and led in Lot to them, and they closed the door.
19.11: And they smote with blindness they that were withoutforth, from the least till to the most; so that they might not find the door.
19.12: Forsooth they said to Lot, Hast thou here any man of thine, husband of thy daughter, or sons, or daughters; if so, lead thou out of this city all men that be thine,
19.13: for we shall do away this place, for the cry of them increased before the Lord, which sent us that we lose them.
19.14: And Lot went out, and spake to the husbands to be of his daughters, that should take his daughters, and said, Rise ye, and go ye out of this place; for the Lord shall do away this city. And he was seen to them to speak as playing.
19.15: And when the morrowtide was, the angels constrained Lot, and said, Rise thou, and take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which thou hast, lest also thou perish altogether in the sin of the city.
19.16: While he dissembled, they took his hand, and the hand of his wife, and of his two daughters; for the Lord spared him. And they led out him, and set [[or put]] him without the city.
19.17: There they spake to him, and said, Save thou thy life; do not thou behold behind thy back, neither stand thou in all the country about, but make thee safe in the hills; lest also thou perish altogether.
19.18: And Lot said to them, My Lord, I beseech,
19.19: for thy servant hath found grace before thee, and thou hast magnified thy grace and mercy, which thou hast done to me, that thou shouldest save my life; I may not be saved in the hills, lest peradventure evil overtake me, and I die;
19.20: a little city is here beside, to which I may flee, and I shall be safe therein; whether it is not such a little city? and my soul shall live therein.
19.21: And he said to Lot, Lo! also in this I have received thy prayers, that I destroy not the city, for which thou hast spoken;
19.22: haste thee, and be thou saved there, for I may not do anything till thou enter [[in]] thither. Therefore the name of that city was called Zoar.
19.23: The sun rose on [[the]] earth, and Lot entered into Zoar.
19.24: Therefore the Lord rained on Sodom and Gomorrah brimstone and fire, from the Lord of heaven,
19.25: and destroyed these cities, and all the country about; he destroyed all the dwellers of those cities, and all green things of [[the]] earth.
19.26: And Lot’s wife looked aback, and she was turned into an image of salt.
19.27: Forsooth Abraham rising early, went to where he stood before with the Lord,
19.28: beheld Sodom and Gomorrah, and all the land of that country; and he saw a dead spark going up from the earth, as the smoke of a furnace.
19.29: For when God destroyed the cities of that country, he had mind of Abraham, and delivered Lot from [[the]] destroying of the cities in which he dwelled.
19.30: And Lot went up from Zoar, and dwelled in the hills, and his two daughters with him, for he dreaded to dwell in Zoar; and he dwelled in a den, he and his two daughters with him.
19.31: And the more daughter said to the less, Our father is eld [[or old]], and no man is left on earth that may enter [[in]] to us, by the custom of all earth;
19.32: come thou, make we him drunken of wine, and sleep we with him, that we may keep the seed of our father.
19.33: And so they gave to their father to drink wine in that night, and the more, or the elder, daughter entered, and slept with her father; and he feeled not, neither when the daughter lay down, neither when she [[a]] rose.
19.34: And the tother day the more daughter said to the less, or the younger, Lo! I slept yesterday with my father; give we to him to drink wine also in this night; and thou sleep with him, that we save the seed of our father.
19.35: And they gave to their father also in that night to drink wine, and the less daughter entered, and slept with him; and soothly he feeled not then when she lay down, neither when she [[a]] rose.
19.36: Therefore the two daughters of Lot conceived of their father.
19.37: And the more daughter childed a son, and called his name Moab; he is the father of men of Moab unto this present day.
19.38: And the less daughter childed a son, and called his name Benammi, that is, The son of my people; he is the father of men of Ammon till to [[this]] day.

20.1: Abraham went forth from thence into the land of the south, and dwelled betwixt Kadesh and Shur, and was a pilgrim in Gerar;
20.2: and he said of Sarah, his wife, She is my sister. Therefore Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent, and took her.
20.3: Soothly God came to Abimelech by a sweven in the night, and said to him, Lo! thou shalt die, for the woman which thou hast taken, for she hath an husband.
20.4: Forsooth Abimelech [[had]] touched not her; and he said, Lord, whether thou shalt slay a folk unknowing and just [[or rightwise]]?
20.5: Whether he said not to me, She is my sister, and she said, He is my brother? In the simpleness of mine heart, and in the cleanness of mine hands, I did this.
20.6: And the Lord said to him, And I know that thou didest by simple heart, and therefore I kept thee, lest thou didest sin against me, and I suffered not that thou touchedest her;
20.7: now therefore yield thou the wife to her husband, for he is a prophet; and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live; soothly if thou wilt not yield her, know thou that thou shalt die by death, thou, and all things that be thine.
20.8: And at once Abimelech rose by night, and called all his servants, and spake all these words in the ears of them; and all men dreaded greatly.
20.9: Soothly Abimelech called also Abraham, and said to him, What hast thou done to us? what sinned we against thee, that thou hast brought in on me and on my realm such a great sin? thou hast done to us which things thou oughtest not to do.
20.10: And again Abimelech asked, and said, What thing sawest thou, that thou wouldest do this?
20.11: Abraham answered, I thought within me, and said, In hap the dread of God is not in this place; and they shall slay me for my wife;
20.12: in other manner forsooth and she is my sister verily, the daughter of my father, and not the daughter of my mother; and I wedded her into wife;
20.13: soothly after that God led me out of the house of my father, I said to her, Thou shalt do this mercy with me in each place to which we shall enter; thou shalt say, that I am thy brother.
20.14: Therefore Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and servants, and handmaids, and gave to Abraham; and he yielded to him Sarah, his wife,
20.15: and said, The land is before you; dwell thou, wherever it pleaseth thee.
20.16: Forsooth Abimelech said to Sarah, Lo! I gave a thousand pieces of silver to thy brother; this shall be to thee into a covering of eyes, to all men that be with thee; and whither ever thou goest, have thou mind that thou art taken.
20.17: Soothly for Abraham prayed, God cured Abimelech, and his wife, and handmaids, and they childed;
20.18: for God had closed each womb of the house of Abimelech, for Sarah, the wife of Abraham.

21.1: Forsooth God visited Sarah, as he promised, and [[ful]] filled those things, that he spake.
21.2: And she conceived, and childed a son in her eld age, in the time wherein God before-said to her.
21.3: And Abraham called the name of his son, whom Sarah childed to him, Isaac.
21.4: And Abraham circumcised him in the eighth day, as God commanded to him,
21.5: when he was of an hundred years; for Isaac was born in this age of the father.
21.6: And Sarah said, The Lord hath made laughing to me, and whoever shall hear shall laugh with me.
21.7: And again she said, Who should hear, and believe to Abraham, that Sarah should give sucking to a son, whom she childed to him, when he is now an eld [[or old]] man?
21.8: Therefore the child increased, and was weaned; and Abraham made a great feast in the day of his weaning.
21.9: And when Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, playing, or doing idolatry, with Isaac her son,
21.10: she said to Abraham, Cast out this handmaid and her son; for the son of the handmaid shall not be heir with my son Isaac.
21.11: Abraham took this heavily for his son;
21.12: and God said to him, Be it not seen sharp to thee on the child, and on thine handmaid; all things which Sarah saith to thee, hear thou her voice, for in Isaac seed shall be called to thee;
21.13: but also I shall make the son of the handmaid into a great folk, for he is thy seed.
21.14: And so Abraham rose early, and took bread, and a bottle of water, and put it on Hagar’s shoulder, and he betook to her the child, and let go her; and when she had gone, she went out of the way in the wilderness of Beersheba.
21.15: And when the water in the bottle was ended, she cast away the child under a tree that was there;
21.16: and she went away, and she sat even against, as far as a bow may cast; for she said, I shall not see the child dying; and she sat against, and raised [[up]] her voice, and wept.
21.17: Forsooth the Lord heard the voice of the child, and the angel of the Lord called Hagar from heaven, and said, What doest thou, Hagar? do not thou dread, for God hath heard the voice of the child, from the place wherein he is.
21.18: Rise thou, and take the child, and hold his hand; for I shall make him into a great folk.
21.19: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water, and she went, and filled the bottle, and she gave drink to the child;
21.20: and God was with him, and he increased, and dwelled in wilderness, and he was made a young man an archer,
21.21: and dwelled in the desert of Paran; and his mother took to him a wife of the land of Egypt.
21.22: In the same time, Abimelech, and Phicol, prince of his host, said to Abraham, God is with thee in all things that thou doest;
21.23: therefore swear thou by God that thou harm not me, and mine heirs, and my kindred; but by the mercy which I did to thee, do thou to me, and to the land in which thou livedest as a comeling.
21.24: And Abraham said, I shall swear.
21.25: And he blamed Abimelech for the well of water, which his servants took away by violence.
21.26: And Abimelech answered, I wist not who did this thing, but also thou showedest not to me, and I heard not except today.
21.27: And so Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave to Abimelech, and both smote together a bond of peace.
21.28: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock asides half.
21.29: And Abimelech said to him, What will these seven ewe lambs mean to themselves, which thou madest stand asides half?
21.30: And he said, Thou shalt take of mine hand seven ewe lambs, that those [[or they]] be into witnessing to me, for I digged this well.
21.31: Therefore that place was called Beersheba, that is, The Well of the Oath, for ever either swore there;
21.32: and they made bond of peace for the well of an oath. Forsooth Abimelech rose, and Phicol, the prince of his chivalry, and they turned again into the land of Palestines.
21.33: Soothly Abraham planted a wood in Beersheba, and inwardly called there the name of [[the]] everlasting God;
21.34: and he was an earth-tiller, or a comeling, of the land of Palestines in many days.

22.1: And after that these things were done, God assayed Abraham, and said to him, Abraham! Abraham! He answered, I am present.
22.2: God said to him, Take thine one begotten son, whom thou lovest, Isaac; and go into the land of vision, and offer thou him there into burnt sacrifice on one of the hills which I shall show to thee.
22.3: Therefore Abraham rose by night, and saddled his ass, and led with him two young men, and Isaac his son; and when he had hewn trees into burnt sacrifice, he went to the place which God had commanded to him.
22.4: Forsooth in the third day, he raised [[up]] his eyes, and saw a place afar;
22.5: and he said to his young men, Abide ye here with the ass, I and the child shall go thither; and after that we have worshipped, we shall turn again to you.
22.6: And he took the wood of burnt sacrifice, and laid it on Isaac his son; forsooth he bare fire, and a sword in his hands. And when they twain [[or two]] went together,
22.7: Isaac said to his father, My father! And he answered, What wilt thou, son? He said, Lo! fire and wood, where is the beast of burnt sacrifice?
22.8: Abraham said, My son, God shall purvey to him the beast of burnt sacrifice. Therefore they went together,
22.9: and came to the place which God had showed to him; in which place Abraham builded an altar, and dressed [[the]] wood above; and when he had bound altogether Isaac, his son, he laid Isaac on the altar, upon the heap of wood.
22.10: And he held forth his hand, and took the sword to sacrifice his son.
22.11: And lo! the angel of the Lord cried from heaven, and said, Abraham! Abraham! Which answered, I am present.
22.12: And the angel said to him, Hold thou not forth thine hand on the child, neither do thou anything of harm to him; now I know that thou dreadest God, and sparedest not thine one begotten son for me.
22.13: Abraham raised [[up]] his eyes, and he saw behind him a ram cleaving by the horns among briars, which he took, and offered as burnt sacrifice for the son.
22.14: And he called the name of that place The Lord seeth; wherefore it is said, till to this day, The Lord shall see in the hill.
22.15: Forsooth the angel of the Lord called to Abraham the second time from heaven,
22.16: and said, The Lord saith, I have sworn by myself, for thou hast done this thing, and hast not spared thine one begotten son for me,
22.17: I shall bless thee, and I shall multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the gravel, either sand, which is in the brink of the sea; thy seed shall wield the gates of his enemies;
22.18: and all the folks of [[the]] earth shall be blessed in thy seed, for thou obeyedest to my voice.
22.19: Abraham turned again to his young men, and they went to Beersheba together, and he dwelled there.
22.20: And so when these things were done, it was told to Abraham that also Milcah had borne sons to Nahor his brother;
22.21: Huz the first begotten, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
22.22: and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel,
22.23: of whom Rebecca was born; Milcah childed these eight to Nahor, the brother of Abraham.
22.24: Forsooth his concubine, or secon-dary wife, Reumah by name, childed Tebah, and Gaham, and Thahash, and Maachah.

23.1: Forsooth Sarah lived an hundred and seven and twenty years,
23.2: and died in the city of Arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan; and Abraham came to bewail and beweep her.
23.3: And when he had risen from the office of the dead body, he spake to the sons of Heth, and said,
23.4: I am a comeling and a pilgrim with you; give ye to me right of [[a]] sepulchre with you, that I bury my dead body.
23.5: And the sons of Heth answered, and said,
23.6: Lord, hear thou us; thou art the prince of God with us; bury thou thy dead body in our chosen sepulchres, and no man shall be able to forbid thee, that not thou bury thy dead body in the sepulchre of him.
23.7: And Abraham [[a]] rose, and worship-ped or honoured the people of the land, that is, the sons of Heth.
23.8: And he said to them, If it pleaseth your soul that I bury my dead body, hear ye me, and pray ye for me to Ephron, the son of Zohar,
23.9: that he give to me the double cave, which he hath in the uttermost part of his field; for sufficient money give he it to me before you into possession of [[a]] sepulchre.
23.10: Forsooth Ephron dwelled in the midst of the sons of Heth. And Ephron answered to Abraham, while all men heard that entered by the gate of that city, and said,
23.11: My lord, it shall not be done so, but more hearken thou to that that I say; I give to thee the field, and the cave which is therein, while the sons of my people be present; bury thou thy dead body.
23.12: Abraham worshipped before the Lord, and before the people of the land,
23.13: and he spake to Ephron, while his people stood about, I beseech, that thou hear me; I shall give money for the field, receive thou it, and so I shall bury my dead body in the field.
23.15: My lord, hear thou me; the land which thou askest for is worth four hundred shekels of silver, that is the price betwixt me and thee; but how much is this? bury thou thy dead body.
23.16: And when Abraham had heard this, he numbered out the money which Ephron asked for, while the sons of Heth heard, four hundred shekels of silver, and of proved common money.
23.17: And the field that was sometime of Ephron, in which field was a double den, beholding to Mamre, as well that field, as the den, and all the trees thereof, in all the terms thereof by compass,
23.18: was confirmed to Abraham into possession, while the sons of Heth saw, and all men that entered by the gate of that city.
23.19: And so Abraham buried Sarah, his wife, in the double den of the field, that beheld to Mamre; this is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
23.20: And the field, and the den that was therein, was confirmed of the sons of Heth to Abraham, into possession of a sepulchre.

24.1: Forsooth Abraham was eld [[or old]], and of many days, and the Lord had blessed him in all things.
24.2: And he said to the elder servant of his house, that was sovereign on all things that he had, Put thou thine hand under mine hip,
