24.3: that I conjure or adjure thee by the Lord God of heaven and of earth, that thou take not a wife to my son of the daughters of Canaan, among which I dwell;
24.4: but that thou go to my land and kindred, and thereof take a wife to my son Isaac.
24.5: The servant answered, If the woman will not come with me into this land, whether I owe to lead again thy son to the place, from which thou wentest out?
24.6: Abraham said, Beware, lest any time thou lead again thither my son;
24.7: the Lord God of heaven that took me from the house of my father, and from the land of my birth, which spake to me, and swore, and said, I shall give this land to thy seed, he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take from thence a wife to my son;
24.8: forsooth if the woman will not follow thee, thou shalt not be holden by the oath; nevertheless lead not again my son thither.
24.9: Therefore the servant putted his hand under the hip of Abraham, his lord, and swore to him on this word.
24.10: And he took ten camels of the flock of his lord, and went forth, and bare with him of all the goods of his lord; and he went forth, and came to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.
24.11: And when he had made the camels to rest without the city, beside a pit or well of water, in the eventide, in that time in which women be wont to go out to draw water,
24.12: he said, Lord God of my lord Abraham, I beseech, meet with me today, and do mercy with my lord Abraham.
24.13: Lo! I stand nigh the well of water, and the daughters of the dwellers of this city shall go out to draw water;
24.14: therefore the damsel to which I shall say, Bow down thy water pot that I drink, and [[she]] shall answer, Drink thou, but also I shall give drink to thy camels, that it is which thou hast made ready to thy servant Isaac; and by this I shall understand that thou hast done mercy to my lord Abraham.
24.15: And he had not yet [[full-]]filled the words within himself, and lo! Rebecca, the daughter of Bethuel, son of Milcah, wife of Nahor, brother of Abraham, went out, having a water pot in her shoulder;
24.16: a damsel full comely/full shapely, and fairest virgin, and unknown of man. Soothly she came down to the well, and filled the water pot, and turned again.
24.17: And the servant met her, and said, Give thou to me a little of the water of thy pot to drink.
24.18: Which answered, Drink thou, my lord. And anon she did down the water pot on her shoulder, and gave drink to him.
24.19: And when he had drunk, she said, But also I shall draw water to thy camels, till all have drunk.
24.20: And she poured out the water pot in[[to]] troughs, and ran again to the pit, to draw water, and she gave water drawn to all the camels.
24.21: Soothly he beheld her privily, and would wit whether the Lord had sped his way, or nay.
24.22: Therefore after that the camels had drunk, the man brought forth golden earrings, weighing two shekels, and as many bands of the arm, in the weight of ten shekels.
24.23: And he said to her, Whose daughter art thou? show thou to me, is [[there]] any place in the house of thy father to dwell in?
24.24: Which answered, I am the daughter of Bethuel, son of Nahor, whom Milcah childed to him.
24.25: And she added, saying, Also full much of provender and of hay is at us, and a large place to dwell in.
24.26: The man bowed himself, and worshipped the Lord,
24.27: and said, Blessed be the Lord God of my lord Abraham, which took not away his mercy and truth from my lord, and led me by the right way, into the house of the brother of my lord.
24.28: And so the damsel ran, and told in the house of her mother all things which she had heard.
24.29: Soothly Rebecca had a brother, Laban by name, which went out hastily to the man, where he was withoutforth.
24.30: And when he had seen the earrings, and bands of the arm in the hands of his sister, and had heard all the words of her, telling, The man spake to me these things, he came to the man that stood beside the camels, and nigh the well of water,
24.31: and said to him, Enter thou, the blessed of the Lord; why standest thou withoutforth? I have made ready the house, and a place to thy camels.
24.32: And he brought him into the inn, and unsaddled the camels, and gave provender, and hay, and water to wash the feet of the camels, and of men that came with him.
24.33: And bread was set forth in his sight, the which said, I shall not eat till I speak my words. He answered to the man, Speak thou.
24.34: And the man said, I am the servant of Abraham,
24.35: and the Lord hath blessed my lord greatly, and he is made great; and God gave to him sheep, and oxen, silver, and gold, servants, and handmaids, and camels, and asses.
24.36: And Sarah, my lord’s wife, childed a son to my lord in his eld age, and Abraham, my lord, hath given all things that he had to that son.
24.37: And my lord charged me greatly, and said, Thou shalt not take to my son a wife of the daughters of Canaan, in whose land I dwell,
24.38: but thou shalt go to the house of my father, and of my kindred thou shalt take a wife to my son.
24.39: Forsooth I answered to my lord, What if the woman will not come with me?
24.40: He said, The Lord, in whose sight I go, shall send his angel with thee, and shall dress thy way; and thou shalt take a wife to my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house.
24.41: Thou shalt be innocent from my curse, when thou comest to my kins-men, and they give not her to thee.
24.42: Therefore I came today to the well of water, and said, Lord God of my lord Abraham, if thou hast dressed my way in which I go now,
24.43: lo! I stand beside the well of water, and the maid[[en]] that shall go out to draw water, heareth me say to her, Give thou to me a little of water to drink of thy pot,
24.44: and she say to me, And thou drink, and I shall draw water to thy camels, that is the woman which the Lord hath made ready to the son of my lord.
24.45: While I turned in thought these things with me, Rebecca appeared, coming with a pot which she bare in her shoulder; and she went down to the well, and drew water. And I said to her, Give thou a little to me to drink;
24.46: and she hasted, and did down the pot off the shoulder, and said to me, And thou drink, and I shall give drink to thy camels; I drank, and she watered the camels.
24.47: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? Which answered, I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, whom Milcah childed to him. And so I hanged earrings to adorn her face, and I put bands of the arm in her hands,
24.48: and low-like I worshipped the Lord, and I blessed the Lord God of my lord Abraham, which God led me by the right way, that I should take the daughter of the brother of my lord to his son.
24.49: Wherefore if ye do mercy and truth with my lord, show ye to me; else if other thing pleaseth, also say ye this, that I go to the right side or to the left side.
24.50: Laban and Bethuel answered, The word is gone out of the Lord; we may not speak any other thing with thee without his pleasance [[or pleasing]].
24.51: Lo! Rebecca is before thee; take thou her, and go forth, and be she [[the]] wife of the son of thy lord, as the Lord spake.
24.52: And when the servant of Abraham had heard this, he felled down, and worshipped the Lord in earth.
24.53: And when vessels of silver, and of gold, and clothes were brought forth, he gave those to Rebecca for a gift, and he gave gifts to her brethren, and mother.
24.54: And when a feast was made, they ate and drank together, and dwelled there. Forsooth the servant rose early, and said, Deliver ye me, that I go to my lord.
24.55: Her brethren and mother answered, The damsel dwell namely ten days at us, and afterward she shall go forth.
24.56: The servant said, Do not ye hold me, for the Lord hath dressed my way; deliver ye me, that I go to my lord.
24.57: And they said, Call we the damsel, and ask we her will.
24.58: And when she was called, and came, they asked her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I shall go.
24.59: Therefore they delivered her, and her nurse, and the servant of Abraham, and his fellows,
24.60: and wished prosperities to their sister, and said, Thou art our sister, increase thou into a thousand thousands, and thy seed wield the gates of his enemies.
24.61: Therefore Rebecca and her damsels ascended [[or went up]] on the camels, and pursued [[or followed]] the man, which turned again hastily to his lord.
24.62: In that time Isaac walked by the way that leadeth to the pit or well, whose name is of him that liveth and seeth; for he dwelled in the south land.
24.63: And he went out to think in the field, for the day was bowed [[down]] then; and when he had raised [[up]] his eyes, he saw camels coming from afar.
24.64: And when Isaac was seen, Rebecca lighted down off the camel,
24.65: and said to the servant, Who is that man that cometh by the field into the meeting of us? And the servant said to her, It is my lord. And she took soon a mantle, and covered herself.
24.66: Forsooth the servant told to his lord Isaac all things which he had done;
24.67: Isaac led her into the tabernacle of Sarah, his mother, and took her to wife; and so much he loved her, that he assuaged the sorrow which befell to him of the death of his mother.

25.1: Forsooth Abraham wedded another wife, Keturah by name,
25.2: which childed to him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
25.3: Also Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. Forsooth the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
25.4: And soothly of Midian was born Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah; all these were the sons of Keturah.
25.5: And Abraham gave all things which he had in possession to Isaac;
25.6: soothly he gave gifts to the sons of [[the]] concubines, that is, secondary wives; and Abraham, while he lived yet, separated them from Isaac, his son, to the east coast.
25.7: Forsooth the days of the life of Abraham were an hundred and threescore and fifteen years;
25.8: and he failed, and died in [[a]] good eld age, and of great age, and full of days, and he was gathered to his people.
25.9: And Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, buried him in the double den, which is set in the field of Ephron, son of Zohar the Hittite, even against Mamre,
25.10: which den he bought of the sons of Heth; and he was buried there, and Sarah his wife.
25.11: And after the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac his son, which dwelled beside the pit by name of him that liveth and seeth.
25.12: These be the generations of Ishmael, the son of Abraham, whom Hagar Egyptian, handmaid of Sarah, childed to Abraham;
25.13: and these be the names of the sons of Ishmael, in their names and generations. The first begotten of Ishmael was Nebajoth, afterward Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
25.14: and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
25.15: and Hadar, and Tema, and Jetur, and Naphish, and Kedemah.
25.16: These were the sons of Ishmael, and these were the names by castles, and towns of them, [[the]] twelve princes of their lineages.
25.17: And the years of [[the]] life of Ishmael were made an hundred and seven and thirty years, and he failed, and died, and was put to his people.
25.18: Forsooth he inhabited from Havilah till to Shur, that beholdeth Egypt, as men entereth into [[the]] Assyrians; he died before all his brethren.
25.19: Also these be the generations of Isaac, the son of Abraham. Abraham begat Isaac,
25.20: and when Isaac was of forty years, he wedded a wife, Rebecca, the daughter of Bethuel, of Syria, of Mesopotamia, the sister of Laban.
25.21: And Isaac besought the Lord for his wife, for she was barren; and the Lord heard him, and gave conceiving to Rebecca.
25.22: But the little children were hurtled together in her womb; and she said, If it was so to coming [[or to come]] to me, what need was it to conceive? And she went to ask counsel of the Lord,
25.23: which answered, and said, Two folks be in thy womb, and two peoples shall be separated from thy womb, and one people shall overturn a people, and the more shall serve the less.
25.24: Then the time of child-bearing came, and lo! two children were found in her womb.
25.25: He that went out first was red, and all rough in the manner of a skin; and his name was called Esau.
25.26: Anon the other went out, and held with his hand the heel of his brother; and therefore he called him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years eld, when the little children were born.
25.27: And when they were waxen, Esau was a man knowing of hunting, and a man an earth-tiller; forsooth Jacob was a simple man, and dwelled in tabernacles.
25.28: Isaac loved Esau, for he ate of the hunting of Esau; and Rebecca loved Jacob.
25.29: Soothly Jacob seethed pottage; and when Esau came weary from the field,
25.30: he said to Jacob, Give thou to me of this red seething, for I am full weary; for which cause his name was called Edom or Red.
25.31: And Jacob said to him, Sell to me the rights of the first begotten child.
25.32: Esau answered, Lo! I die, what shall the first begotten things profit to me?
25.33: Jacob said, Therefore swear thou to me. Therefore Esau swore, and sold the first engendered things.
25.34: And so when he had taken bread and pottage, Esau ate and drank, and went forth, and charged or cared little that he had sold the rights of the first begotten child.

26.1: Forsooth for hunger rose on the land, after that barrenness that befelled in the days of Abraham, Isaac went forth to Abimelech, king of Palestines, in Gerar.
26.2: And the Lord appeared to him, and said, Go not down into Egypt, but rest thou in the land which I shall say to thee,
26.3: and be thou a pilgrim therein; and I shall be with thee, and I shall bless thee; for I shall give all these countries to thee, and to thy seed, and I shall [[ful]] fill the oath which I promised to Abraham, thy father.
26.4: And I shall multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and I shall give all these countries to thine heirs, and all folks of the earth shall be blessed in thy seed,
26.5: for Abraham obeyed to my voice, and kept my behests, and my commandments, and my ceremonies, and my laws.
26.6: And so Isaac dwelled in Gerar.
26.7: And when he was asked of [[the]] men of that place of his wife, he answered, She is my sister; for he dreaded to acknowledge that she was fellowshipped to him in matrimony, and he guessed lest peradventure they would slay him for the fairness of her.
26.8: And when full many days were passed, and he dwelled there, Abimelech, king of Palestines, beheld by a window, and saw him playing with Rebecca, his wife.
26.9: And when Isaac was called, the king said, It is open, that she is thy wife; why saidest thou, that she was thy sister? Isaac answered, For I dreaded, lest I should die for her.
26.10: And Abimelech said, Why hast thou deceived us? Some man of the people might do lechery with thy wife, and thou haddest brought in grievous sin on us.
26.11: And the king commanded to all the people, and said, He that toucheth the wife of this man shall die by death.
26.12: Forsooth Isaac sowed in that land, and he found an hundredfold increase in that year; and the Lord blessed him.
26.13: And the man was made rich, and he went profiting and increasing, till he was made full great.
26.14: Also he had possessions of sheep and of great beasts, and full much of menials. For this thing Palestines had envy to him,
26.15: and they stopped in that time and filled with earth all the pits or wells which the servants of Abraham his father had digged,
26.16: in so much that Abimelech himself said to Isaac, Go thou away from us, for thou art made greatly mightier than we.
26.17: And he went away, that he should come to the strand of Gerar, and dwelled there.
26.18: And he digged again other wells, which the servants of Abraham his father had digged, and which the Philistines had stopped sometime, when Abraham was dead; and he called those pits by the same names, by which his father had called before.
26.19: They digged in the strand, and they found quick, or welling up, water.
26.20: But also strife of [[the]] shepherds of Gerar was there against the shep-herds of Isaac, and they said, The water is ours; wherefore of that strife that befelled, Isaac called the name of that well False Challenge, or Esek, or Quarrel.
26.21: And they digged another well, and they strived also for that, and Isaac called that well Enmities, or Sitnah, or Enmity.
26.22: And he went forth from thence, and digged another pit, for which they strived not, [[and]] therefore he called the name of that well Breadth, either Largeness; and said, Now God hath alarged us, and hath made us to increase on [[the]] earth.
26.23: Isaac forsooth went up from that place into Beersheba,
26.24: where the Lord appeared to him in that night; and said, I am [[the]] God of Abraham, thy father; do not thou dread, for I am with thee, and I shall bless thee, and I shall multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham.
26.25: And so Isaac builded there an altar to the Lord; and when the name of the Lord was inwardly called, he stretched forth a tabernacle; and he commanded his servants that they should dig pits.
26.26: And when Abimelech, and Ahuzzath, one of his friends, and Phicol, [[the]] duke of knights, had come from Gerar to that place,
26.27: Isaac spake to them, What came ye to me, a man whom ye have hated, and putted away from you?
26.28: Which answered, We saw that God is with thee, and therefore we said now, An oath be betwixt us, and make we a covenant of peace,
26.29: that thou do not any [[thing of]] evil to us, as we touched nothing of thine, neither did that that hurted thee, but with peace we let go thee increased by the blessings of the Lord.
26.30: Therefore Isaac made them a feast; and after meat and drink,
26.31: they rose early, and swore each to other; and Isaac let go them peaceably into their place.
26.32: Lo! forsooth in that day the servants of Isaac came, telling to him of the pit which they had digged, and said, We have found water.
26.33: Wherefore Isaac called that pit Abundance or Shebah; and the name of the city was set Beersheba till into this present day.
26.34: Esau forsooth forty years eld [[or old]] wedded two wives, Judith, the daughter of Beeri Hittite, and Bashemath, the daughter of Elon, of the same place;
26.35: which both offended the soul of Isaac and of Rebecca.

27.1: Forsooth Isaac waxed eld [[or old]], and his eyes dimmed, and he might not see. And he called Esau, his more or older son, and said to him, My son! Which answered, I am present.
27.2: To whom the father said, Thou seest that I have waxed eld, and I know not the day of my death.
27.3: Take thine arms, an arrow case, and a bow, and go out; and when thou hast taken anything by hunting,
27.4: make me a stew thereof, as thou knowest that I will or desire, and bring it to me that I eat, that my soul bless thee before that I die.
27.5: And when Rebecca had heard this thing, and he had gone forth into the field that he fulfill the behest of his father,
27.6: she said to her son Jacob, I heard thy father speaking with Esau, thy brother, and saying to him,
27.7: Bring thou to me of thine hunting, and make thou meats, that I eat, and that I bless thee before the Lord before that I die.
27.8: Now therefore, my son, assent to my counsels,
27.9: and go to the flock, and bring to me twain [[or two]] of the best kids, that I make meats of those to thy father, which he shall eat gladly;
27.10: and that when thou hast brought in those meats, and he hath eaten, he bless thee before that he die.
27.11: To whom Jacob answered, Thou knowest that Esau my brother is an hairy man, and I am smooth;
27.12: if my father shall touch or draw me to him, and feel me, I dread lest he guess that I would scorn him, and he bring in cursing on me for blessing.
27.13: To whom his mother said, My son, this cursing be in me; only hear thou my voice, and go, and bring that that I said.
27.14: He went, and brought it, and gave it to his mother. She made ready meats, as she knew that his father would have,
27.15: and she clothed Jacob in [[the]] full good clothes of Esau, which she had at home with herself.
27.16: And she wrapped his hands about with little skins of goat kids, and covered the nakedness of his neck;
27.17: and she gave to him the stew, and betook him [[the]] loaves, which she had baked.
27.18: And when these were brought in, he said, My father! And he answered, I am here; who art thou, my son?
27.19: And Jacob said, I am Esau, thy first begotten son. I have done to thee as thou commandedest to me; rise thou up, and sit, and eat of my venison, that thy soul bless me.
27.20: Again Isaac said to his son, My son, how mightest thou find this venison so soon? Which answered, It was God’s will, that this thing that I would, should come soon to me.
27.21: And Isaac said, My son, come thou hither, that I touch thee, and that I prove whether thou be my son Esau, or nay.
27.22: Jacob nighed to his father; and when Isaac had feeled him, he said, Soothly the voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands be the hands of Esau.
27.23: And Isaac knew not Jacob, for the hairy hands showed the likeness of the elder son. Therefore Isaac blessed Jacob,
27.24: and said again, Art thou my son Esau? Jacob answered, I am.
27.25: And Isaac said, My son, bring thou to me meats of thine hunting, that my soul bless thee. And when Isaac had eaten these meats brought, Jacob brought also wine to Isaac, and when this was drunken,
27.26: Isaac said to him, My son, come thou hither, and give to me a kiss.
27.27: Jacob nighed, and kissed him; and anon as Isaac feeled the odour of his clothes, he blessed him, and said, Lo! the odour of my son as the odour of a plenteous field which the Lord hath blessed.
27.28: God give to thee of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of [[the]] earth, abundance [[or plenty]] of wheat, and of wine, and of oil;
27.29: and peoples serve thee, and lineages worship thee; be thou lord of thy brethren, and the sons of thy mother be bowed before thee; be he cursed that curseth thee, and he that blesseth thee, be he [[full-]]filled with blessings.
27.30: Scarcely Isaac had filled the word, and when Jacob was gone out, Esau came,
27.31: and brought in meats sodden of the hunting to the father, and said, My father, rise thou, and eat of the hunting of thy son, that thy soul bless me.
27.32: And Isaac said, Who art thou? Which answered, I am Esau, thy first begotten son.
27.33: Isaac dreaded with a great aston-ishing; and he wondered more than it may be believed, and said, Who therefore is he which a while ago brought to me venison taken, and I ate of all things before that thou camest; and I blessed him? and he shall be blessed.
27.34: When the words of the father were heard, Esau roared with a great cry, and was astonied, and said, My father, bless thou also me.
27.35: Which said, Thy brother came prudently [[or beguilingly]], and took thy blessing.
27.36: And Esau added, Justly his name is called Jacob, for lo! he [[hath]] supplanted me another time; before he took away my first begotten things, and now the second time, he [[hath]] ravished privily my blessing. And again he said to the father, Whether thou hast not reserved a blessing also to me?
27.37: Isaac answered, I have made him thy lord, and I have made subject all his brethren to his servage; I have stablished him in wheat, and wine, and oil; and so, my son, what shall I do to thee after these things?
27.38: To whom Esau said, Father, whether thou hast only one blessing? I beseech thee, that also thou bless me. And when Esau wept with great yelling,
27.39: Isaac was stirred, and said to him, Thy blessing shall not be in the fatness of [[the]] earth, and in the dew of heaven from above;
27.40: thou shalt live by sword, and thou shalt serve thy brother, and time shall come when thou shalt shake away, and unbind his yoke from [[off]] thy nolls.
27.41: Therefore Esau hated evermore Jacob for the blessing by which the father had blessed him; and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning of my father shall come, and I shall slay Jacob, my brother.
27.42: These things were told to Rebecca, and she sent, and called her son Jacob, and said to him, Lo! Esau, thy brother, menaceth [[or threateneth]] to slay thee;
27.43: now therefore, my son, hear thou my voice, and rise thou up, and flee to Laban, my brother, into Haran;
27.44: and thou shalt dwell with him a few days, till the strong vengeance of thy brother rest, and his indignation cease,
27.45: and till he forget those things which thou hast done against him. Afterward I shall send, and I shall bring thee from thence hither. Why shall I be made sonless of ever either son in one day?
27.46: And Rebecca said to Isaac, It annoyeth or vexeth me of my life for the daughters of Heth; if Jacob take a wife of the kindred of this land, I will not live.

28.1: And so Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and commanded to him, and said, Do not thou take a wife of the kin of Canaan;
28.2: but go thou, and walk forth into Mesopotamia of Syria, to the house of Bethuel, [[the]] father of thy mother, and take to thee from thence a wife of the daughters of Laban, thine uncle.
28.3: Soothly Almighty God bless thee, and make thee to increase, and multiply thee, that thou be into companies of peoples;
28.4: and God give to thee the blessing of Abraham, and to thy seed after thee, that thou wield the land of thy pilgrimage, which he promised to thy grand-sire.
28.5: And when Isaac had let go Jacob, he went forth, and came into Mesopotamia of Syria, to Laban, the son of Bethuel of Syria, the brother of Rebecca, his mother.
28.6: Forsooth Esau saw that his father had blessed Jacob, and had sent him into Mesopotamia of Syria, that he should wed a wife of thence, and that after the blessing he commanded to Jacob, and said, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
28.7: and that Jacob obeyed to his father and mother, and went into Syria;
28.8: also Esau proved thereby that his father beheld not gladly the daughters of Canaan.
28.9: And Esau went to Ishmael, and wedded a wife, without these which he had before, Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, son of Abraham, the sister of Nebajoth.
28.10: Therefore Jacob went out of Beersheba, and went to Haran.
28.11: And when he had come to some place, and would rest therein after the going down of the sun, he took of the stones that lay there, and he put under his head, and slept in the same place.
28.12: And he saw in [[his]] sleep a ladder standing on the earth, and the top thereof touching heaven; and he saw God’s angels ascending or going up and going down thereby,
28.13: and the Lord nighed to the ladder, saying to him, I am the Lord God of Abraham, thy father, and God of Isaac; I shall give to thee and to thy seed the land in which thou sleepest.
28.14: And thy seed shall be as the dust of [[the]] earth, thou shalt be alarged to the east, and west, and to the north, and south; and all the lineages of [[the]] earth shall be blessed in thee and in thy seed.
28.15: And I shall be thy keeper, whither ever thou shalt go; and I shall lead thee again into this land, and I shall not leave thee, no but I shall fulfill all [[the]] things which I have said.
28.16: And when Jacob had waked of [[the]] sleep, he said, Verily the Lord is in this place, and I knew not.
28.17: And he said dreading, How fearedful, or worshipful, is this place! Here is none other thing, no but the house of God, and the gate of heaven.
28.18: Therefore Jacob rose early, and took the stone which he had put under his head, and raised it up into a title, or sign, and poured out oil above.
28.19: And he called the name of that city Bethel, which was called Luz before.
28.20: Also Jacob avowed a vow, and said, If God is with me, and keepeth me in the way in which I go, and giveth to me loaves to eat, and clothes to be clothed with,
28.21: and I turn again in prosperity to the house of my father, the Lord shall be into God to me.
28.22: And this stone, which I raised into a title, shall be called the house of God; and I shall offer tithes to thee of all things which thou shalt give to me.

29.1: Therefore Jacob passed forth, and came into the east land;
29.2: and he saw a pit or well in the field, and three flocks of sheep resting beside it, for why sheep were watered thereof, and the mouth thereof was closed with a great stone.
29.3: And the custom was that when all the sheep were gathered together, they should turn away the stone, and when the flocks were watered, they should put it again on the mouth of the pit.
29.4: And Jacob said to the shepherds, Brethren, of whence be ye? Which answered, Of Haran.
29.5: And he asked them and said, Whether ye know Laban, the son of Nahor? They said, We know him.
29.6: Jacob said, Is he whole? They said, He is in good state; and lo! Rachel, his daughter, cometh with his flock.
29.7: And Jacob said, Yet much of the day is to come, and it is not time that the flocks be led again to the folds; soothly give ye drink to the sheep, and so lead ye them again to meat or feeding.
29.8: Which answered, We may not till all the sheep be gathered together, and till we remove the stone from the mouth of the pit, to water the flocks.
29.9: Yet they spake, and lo! Rachel came with the sheep of her father.
29.10: And when Jacob saw her, and knew her to be the daughter of his mother’s brother, and the sheep to be of Laban his uncle, he removed the stone with which the pit was closed; and when the flock was watered,
29.11: he kissed her, and he wept with voice raised.
29.12: And Jacob showed to her that he was the brother of her father, and the son of Rebecca; and she hasted, and told to her father.
29.13: And when he had heard, that Jacob, the son of his sister, came, he ran to meet him, and he embraced Jacob, and kissed him, and led him into his house. Forsooth when the causes of the journey were heard,
29.14: Laban answered, Thou art my bone and my flesh. And after that the days of a month were filled,
29.15: Laban said to Jacob, Whether for thou art my brother, thou shalt serve me freely? say thou what meed thou shalt take.
29.16: Forsooth Laban had two daughters, the name of the elder was Leah, soothly the younger was called Rachel;
29.17: but Leah was bleary-eyed, and Rachel was of fair face, and lovely in sight.
29.18: And Jacob loved Rachel, and said, I shall serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
29.19: Laban answered, It is better that I give her to thee than to another man; dwell thou with me.
29.20: Therefore Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and the days seemed few to him for the greatness of his love.
29.21: And at last he said to Laban, Give thou my wife to me, for the time is fulfilled that I enter [[in]] to her.
29.22: And when many companies of friends were called to the feast, he made [[the]] weddings,
29.23: and in the eventide Laban brought in to him Leah his daughter,
29.24: and gave an handmaid, Zilpah by name, to his daughter.
29.25: And when Jacob had entered [[in]] to her by custom, when the morrow-tide was made, he saw Leah, and he said to his wife’s father, What is it that thou wouldest do? whether I served not thee for Rachel? why hast thou deceived me?
29.26: Laban answered, It is not custom in our place that we give first the younger daughter to weddings;
29.27: fulfill thou the week of days of this wedding, and I shall give to thee also this Rachel, for the work in which thou shalt serve me by other seven years.
29.28: Jacob assented to the covenant, and when the week was passed, he wedded Rachel,
29.29: to whom her father had given Bilhah an handmaid.
29.30: And at the last Jacob used the weddings desired, and set the love of the latter wife before the first; and Jacob served Laban seven other years.
29.31: Forsooth the Lord saw that Jacob despised Leah, that is, loved her less than Rachel, and he opened Leah’s womb, while her sister dwelled barren.
29.32: And Leah childed a son conceived, and she called his name Reuben, and said, The Lord hath seen my meek-ness; now mine husband shall love me.
29.33: And again she conceived, and childed a son, and said, For the Lord saw that I was despised, he gave also this son to me; and she called his name Simeon.
29.34: And she conceived the third time, and childed another son, and she said also, Now mine husband shall be coupled to me, for I have childed three sons to him; and therefore she called his name Levi.
29.35: The fourth time she conceived, and childed a son, and said, Now I shall acknowledge to the Lord; and therefore she called his name Judah; and ceased to child.

30.1: Forsooth Rachel saw, that she was unfruitful, and she had envy to her sister, and said to her husband, Give thou free children to me, else I shall die.
30.2: To whom Jacob was wroth, and answered, Whether I am for God, which have deprived thee from the fruit of thy womb?
30.3: And she said, I have an handmaid Bilhah; enter thou [[in]] to her that she child on my knees, and that I have sons of her.
30.4: And she gave to him Bilhah into matrimony; and when her husband had entered [[in]] to her,
30.5: she conceived, and childed a son.
30.6: And Rachel said, The Lord hath deemed to me, and hath heard my prayer, and gave a son to me; and therefore she called his name Dan.
30.7: And again Bilhah conceived, and childed another son,
30.8: for whom Rachel said, The Lord hath made me like my sister, and I [[have]] waxed strong; and she called him Naphtali.
30.9: Leah feeled that she ceased to bear child, and she gave Zilpah, her handmaid, to her husband.
30.10: And when Zilpah, after conceiving, childed a son,
30.11: Leah said, Blessedly; and therefore she called his name Gad.
30.13: and Leah said, This is for my bliss, for all women shall say me blessed; therefore she called him Asher.
30.14: Forsooth Reuben went out into the field in the time of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes, which he brought to Leah, his mother. And Rachel said, Give thou to me a part of the mandrakes of thy son.
30.15: Leah answered, Whether it seemeth little to thee, that thou hast ravished my husband from me, no but thou take also the mandrakes of my son? Rachel said, The husband sleep with thee in this night for the mandrakes of thy son.
30.16: And when Jacob came again from the field at the eventide, Leah went out into his meeting, and said, Thou shalt enter [[in]] to me, for I have hired thee with hire for the mandrakes of my son. He slept with her in that night;
30.17: and God heard her prayers, and she conceived, and childed the fifth son;
30.18: and said, God hath given meed to me, for I gave mine handmaid to mine husband; and she called his name Issachar.
30.19: Again Leah conceived, and childed the sixth son,
30.20: and said, The Lord hath made me rich with a good dower; also in this time mine husband shall be with me, for I have engendered six sons to him; and therefore she called his name Zebulun.
30.21: After whom she childed a daughter, Dinah by name.
30.22: Also the Lord had mind on Rachel, and he heard her, and opened her womb.
30.23: And she conceived, and childed a son, and said, God hath taken away my shame;
30.24: and she called his name Joseph, and said, The Lord give to me another son.
30.25: Soothly when Joseph was born, Jacob said to his wife’s father, Deliver thou me, that I turn again to my country, and to my land.
30.26: Give thou to me my wives, and my free children, for which I have served thee, that I go; forsooth thou knowest the service by which I have served thee.
30.27: Laban said to him, Find I grace in thy sight; I have learned by experience, that God hath blessed me for thee;
30.28: ordain thou the meed which I shall give to thee.
30.29: And Jacob answered, Thou knowest how I have served thee, and how great thy possession was in mine hands;
30.30: thou haddest little before that I came to thee, and now thou art made rich, and the Lord [[hath]] blessed thee at mine entering; therefore it is just that I purvey sometime also for mine house.
30.31: And Laban said, What shall I give to thee? And Jacob said, I will or desire nothing, that is, of thy gift, but if thou doest that that I ask, again I shall feed and keep thy sheep.
30.32: Go about all thy flocks, and separate thou all diversely-coloured sheep, and of spotted fleeces, and whatever thing shall be of dun hue, and spotted, and diverse of colour, as well in sheep as in goats; that shall be my meed.
30.33: And my rightfulness [[or rightwise-ness]] shall answer to me tomorrow, when the time of covenant shall come before thee; and all that be not diverse, and spotted, and dunned, as well in sheep as in goats, be found at me thou shalt reprove me of theft.
30.34: And Laban said, I have it acceptable that that thou askest.
30.35: And Laban separated in that day [[the]] goats, and sheep, goat bucks, and rams, diverse and spotted. Soothly he betook all the flock of one colour, that is, of white, and of black fleece, into the hands of his sons;
30.36: and he set the space of a way of three days betwixt his sons, and the husband of his daughters, that fed his other flocks.
30.37: Therefore Jacob took green rods of poplars, and of almonds, and of planes, and in part he did away the rind of them; and when the rinds were drawn away, either shaved, whiteness appeared in these that were made bare; soothly those that were whole dwelled green, and by this manner the colour was made diverse.
30.38: And Jacob put those rods in the troughs, where the water was poured out, that when the flocks should come to drink,
30.39: they should have the rods before their eyes, and they should conceive in [[the]] sight of the rods. And it was done that in that heat of riding, or engendering, the sheep should behold those rods, and that they should bring forth spotted beasts, and diverse, and besprinkled with diverse colour.
30.40: And Jacob separated the flock, and put the rods in the [[water]] troughs, before the eyes of the rams. Soothly all the white and [[the]] black were Laban’s; soothly all the others were Jacob’s; for the flocks were separated betwixt themselves.
30.41: Therefore when the sheep were ridden in the first time, Jacob put the rods in the water troughs before the eyes of rams, and of ewe sheep, that they should conceive in the sight of the rods.
30.42: Forsooth when the late mixing, or engendering, and the last conceivings were, Jacob put not those rods; and those that were late engendered, were made Laban’s, and those that were of the first time engendered, were Jacob’s.
30.43: And Jacob was made full rich, and had many flocks, handmaids, and menservants, camels, and asses.

31.1: After that, Jacob heard the words of the sons of Laban, that said, Jacob hath taken away all things that were our father’s, and of his chattel Jacob is made rich, and noble.
31.2: Also Jacob perceived the face of Laban, that it was not against him as yesterday, and the third day ago,
31.3: mostly for the Lord said to Jacob, Turn again into the land of thy fathers, and to thy generation, and I shall be with thee.
31.4: Jacob sent, and called Rachel and Leah into the field, where he kept [[the]] flocks,
31.5: and he said to them, I see the face of your father, that it is not against me as yesterday, and the third day ago; but God of my father was with me.
31.6: And ye know that with all my strengths I have served your father;
31.7: but and your father hath deceived me, and changed my meed ten times; and nevertheless God suffered not him to annoy me.
31.8: If he said any time, Diversely-coloured sheep shall be thy meed, all the sheep brought forth diversely-coloured lambs; forsooth when he said, on the contrary, Thou shalt take all the white for thy meed, all the flocks brought forth white beasts;
31.9: and God took away the substance of your father, and gave it to me.
31.10: For after that the time of con-ceiving of sheep came, I raised [[up]] mine eyes, and saw in sleep males diverse, and spotty, and of diverse colours, going up on females.
31.11: And the angel of the Lord said to me in sleep, Jacob! and I answered, I am ready.
31.12: Which said, Raise [[up]] thine eyes, and see all [[the]] males that be diverse, [[and]] besprinkled, and spotty, going [[up]] on [[the]] females; for I have seen all things which Laban hath done to thee;
31.13: I am God of Bethel, where thou anointedest a stone, and madest a vow to me. Now therefore rise thou, and go out of this land, and turn again into the land of thy birth.
31.14: And Rachel and Leah answered, Whether we have anything residue, or left, in the chattels, and heritage of our father?
31.15: Whether he areckoned not, or held, us as aliens, and sold us, and ate our price?
31.16: But God took away the riches of our father, and gave those [[or them]] to us, and to our sons; wherefore do thou all things which God hath commanded to thee.
31.17: Forsooth Jacob rose, and put his free children and wives on camels, and went forth;
31.18: and he took all his cattle, flocks, and whatever thing he had gotten in Mesopotamia, and went to Isaac, his father, into the land of Canaan.
31.19: In that time Laban went to shear sheep, and Rachel stole the idols of her father.
31.20: And Jacob would not acknowledge to the father of his wives, that he would flee;
31.21: and when he had gone, as well he as all things that were of his right, and when he had passed [[over]] the water, and he went against the hill of Gilead,
31.22: it was told to Laban, in the third day, that Jacob fled.
31.23: And Laban took his brethren [[with him]], and pursued him seven days, and [[over]] took him in the hill of Gilead.
31.24: And Laban saw in sleep the Lord saying to him, Beware that thou speak not anything sharply against Jacob.
31.25: And then Jacob had stretched forth the tabernacle in the hill; and when Laban had pursued Jacob with his brethren, Laban set a tent in the same hill of Gilead;
31.26: and he said to Jacob, Why hast thou done so, that the while I knew not, thou wouldest drive away my daughters as captives, either taken prisoners, by sword?
31.27: Why wouldest thou flee the while I knew not, neither wouldest show to me, that I should pursue [[or follow]] thee with joy, and songs, and tympans, and harps?
31.28: Thou sufferedest not that I should kiss my sons and daughters; thou hast wrought follily.
31.29: And now soothly mine hand may yield evil to thee, but the God of thy father said to me yesterday, Beware that thou speak not any hard thing with Jacob.
31.30: Suppose, if thou covetedest to go to thy kinsmen, and the house of thy father was in desire to thee, why hast thou stolen my gods?
31.31: Jacob answered, That I went forth while thou knewest not, I dreaded lest thou wouldest take away thy daughters from me violently;
31.32: soothly that thou reprovest me of theft, at whomever thou findest thy gods, be he slain before our brethren; seek thou, whatever thing of thine thou findest at me, and take it away. Jacob said these things, and knew not that Rachel had stolen the idols.
31.33: And so Laban entered into the tabernacles of Jacob, and of Leah, and of ever either menial, and he found not; and when Laban had entered into the tent of Rachel,
31.34: she hasted, and hid the idols under the strewings of the camel, and she sat above.
31.35: And she said to Laban, seeking throughout all the tent, and finding nothing, My lord, be not wroth that I may not rise before thee, for it befelled now to me by the custom of women; so the busyness of the seeker was scorned.
31.36: And Jacob swelled, and said with strife, For what cause of me, and for what sin of me, hast thou come so fiercely after me,
31.37: and hast sought through all the appurtenance of mine house? What hast thou found of all the chattel of thine household? Put thou here before my brethren and thy brethren, and deem they betwixt me and thee.
31.38: Was I not with thee therefore twenty years? Thy sheep and goats were not barren, I ate not the rams of thy flock,
31.39: neither I showed to thee anything taken of a beast; I yielded all [[the]] harm; whatever thing perished by theft, thou askedest of me;
31.40: I was anguished in day and night with heat and frost, and sleep fled from mine eyes;
31.41: so I served thee by twenty years in thine house, fourteen years for thy daughters, and six years for thy flocks; and thou changedest my meed ten times.
31.42: But if [[the]] God of my father Abraham, and the dread of Isaac had not helped me, peradventure now thou haddest left me naked; the Lord hath beheld my tormenting and the travail of mine hands, and reproved thee yesterday.
31.43: Laban answered to Jacob, The daughters, and the sons, and the flocks, and all things which thou seest, be mine; what may I do to my sons, and to the sons of my sons?
31.44: Therefore come thou, and make we bond of peace, that it be a witnessing betwixt me and thee.
31.45: And so Jacob took a stone, and raised it into a title, either a sign,
31.46: and said to his brethren, Bring ye stones; which gathered, and made an heap, and ate on it.
31.47: And Laban called it The heap of witness, and Jacob called it The heap of witnessing; ever either called it by the property of his language.
31.48: And Laban said, This heap shall be witness betwixt me and thee today, and therefore the name thereof was called Galeed, that is, The heap of witness.
31.49: And Laban added, The Lord behold, and deem betwixt us, when we shall go away from you;
31.50: if thou shalt torment my daughters, and if thou shalt bring in other wives on them, none is witness of our word, except God, which is present, and beholdeth.
31.51: And again Laban said to Jacob, Lo! this heap, and the stone, or the pillar, which I have raised betwixt me and thee,
31.52: shall be witnesses; soothly this heap, and the stone be into witnessing, forsooth if I shall pass it, and go to thee, either thou shalt pass it, and think to do evil to me.
31.53: God of Abraham, and God of Nahor, [[the]] God of the father of them, deem betwixt us. Therefore Jacob swore by the dread of his father Isaac;
31.54: and when slain sacrifices were offered in the hill, Jacob called his brethren to eat bread, and when they had eaten, they dwelled there.
31.55: Forsooth Laban rose by night, and kissed his sons, and daughters, and blessed them, and turned again into his place.

32.1: Forsooth Jacob went forth in the way in which he began, and the angels of the Lord met him.
32.2: And when he had seen them, he said, These be the castles of God; and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
32.3: Soothly Jacob sent before him also messengers to Esau, his brother, into the land of Seir, in the country of Edom;
32.4: and he commanded to them, and said, Thus speak ye to my lord Esau, Thy brother Jacob saith these things, I have been a pilgrim at Laban, and I was till into this present day;
32.5: I have oxen, and asses, and sheep, and menservants, and handmaids, and I send now a message to my lord, that I find grace in thy sight.
32.6: And the messengers turned again to Jacob, and said, We came to Esau, thy brother, and lo! he hasteth him into thy coming, with four hundred men.
32.7: Jacob dreaded greatly, and he was afeared, and he parted the people that was with him, and he parted the flocks, and sheep, and oxen, and camels, into two companies;
32.8: and he said, If Esau shall come to one company, and shall smite it, the other company which is left unsmitten, shall be saved.
32.9: And Jacob said, O! God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O! Lord, that saidest to me, Turn thou again into thy land, and to the place of thy birth, and I shall do well to thee,
32.10: I am less than all thy merciful doings, and than thy truth which thou hast [[ful]] filled to thy servant; with my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I go again with two companies;
32.11: deliver thou me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I dread him greatly, lest he come and smite or slay the mothers with the sons [[or with the children]].
32.12: Thou spakest that thou shouldest do well to me, and wouldest alarge my seed as [[the]] gravel of the sea, that may not be numbered for muchliness.
32.13: And when Jacob had slept there in that night, he separated of those things which he had as gifts to Esau, his brother,
32.14: two hundred she goats, and twenty bucks of goats, two hundred sheep, and twenty rams,
32.15: camels full with their foals thirty, forty kine, and twenty bulls, twenty she-asses, and [[the]] ten foals of them.
32.16: And he sent by the hands of his servants all the flocks by themselves; and he said to his servants, Go ye before me, and a space be betwixt flock and flock.
32.17: And he commanded to the former or first, and said, If thou shalt meet my brother Esau, and he shall ask thee, whose man thou art, or whither thou goest, or whose be these things which thou followest,
32.18: thou shalt answer, Of thy servant Jacob; he hath sent gifts to his lord Esau, and he cometh after us.
32.19: In like manner, he gave command-ments to the second, and to the third, and to all that pursued [[or followed]] the flocks; and said, Speak ye by the same words to Esau, when ye find him,
32.20: and ye shall add, Also Jacob himself thy servant pursueth [[or followeth]] our way. For Jacob said, I shall please Esau with gifts that go before, and afterward I shall see him; in hap he shall be merciful to me.
32.21: And so the gifts went before him; soothly he dwelled in that night in the tents.
32.22: And when Jacob had risen hastily, he took his two wives, and so many handmaids, with his eleven sons, and he passed over the ford of Jabbok.
32.23: And when all things that pertained to him were led over,
32.24: Jacob dwelled there alone, and, lo! a man came, and wrestled with him till to the morrowtide.
32.25: And when the man saw that he might not overcome Jacob, he touched the sinew of Jacob’s hip, and it dried anon.
32.26: And he said to Jacob, Let go thou me, for the morrowtide goeth up now. Jacob answered, I shall not let go thee, no but thou bless me.
32.27: Therefore he said, What name is to thee? He answered, Jacob.
32.28: And the man said, Thy name shall no more be called Jacob, but Israel; for if thou were strong against God, how much more shalt thou have power against men.
32.29: Jacob asked him, Say thou to me by what name thou art called? He answered, Why askest thou my name, which is wonderful? And he blessed Jacob in the same place.
32.30: And Jacob called the name of that place Penuel, and said, I saw the Lord face to face, and my life is made safe.
32.31: And anon the sun rose to him, after that he had passed over from Penuel; forsooth he halted in the foot.
32.32: For which cause the sons of Israel eat not unto this present day the sinew, like that that dried in the hip of Jacob; for the man touched the sinew of Jacob’s hip, and it dried up.

33.1: Forsooth Jacob raised up his eyes, and saw Esau coming, and four hundred men with him; and he parted the sons of Leah, and of Rachel, and of both the servantesses.
33.2: And he put ever either handmaid, and the free children of them, in the beginning; soothly he put Leah, and her sons, in the second place; forsooth he put Rachel and Joseph the last.
33.3: And Jacob went before, and worshipped or honoured lowly to the earth seven times, till his brother nighed.
33.4: And so Esau ran against his brother, and embraced him, and Esau held his neck, and kissed him, and wept.
33.5: And when Esau’s eyes were raised up, he saw the women, and the little children of them, and said, What will these mean to themselves? and whether they pertain to thee? Jacob answered, They be the little children, which God hath given to me, thy servant.
33.6: And the handmaids and their sons nighed, and were bowed.
33.7: Also Leah nighed with her free children; and when they had worshipped in like manner, Joseph and Rachel last worshipped.
33.8: And Esau said, What be these companies, which I met? And Jacob answered, That I should find grace before my lord.
33.9: And he said, My brother, I have full many things, thy things be to thee.
33.10: And Jacob said, I beseech thee, do not thou so, but if I have found grace in thine eyes, take thou a little gift of mine hands; for I saw so thy face as if I had seen the cheer of God; be thou merciful to me,
33.11: and receive the blessing which I have brought to thee, and which blessing God giving all things gave to me. Scarcely desiring it, while the brother compelled, he received,
33.12: and said, Go we together, and I shall be a fellow of thy way.
33.13: And Jacob said, My lord, thou knowest that I have little children tender, and sheep, and kine with calves with me, and if I shall make them for to travail more in going, all the flocks shall die in one day;
33.14: my lord go before his servant, and I shall pursue [[or follow]] little and little his steps, as I see that my little children be able, till I come to my lord, into Seir.
33.15: Esau answered, I pray thee, that of the people which is with me, dwell they namely fellows of thy way. Jacob said, It is no need; I have need to this one thing only, that I find grace in thy sight, my lord.
33.16: And so Esau turned again in that day in the way by which he came, into Seir.
33.17: And Jacob came into Succoth, where when he had builded an house, and had set tents, he called the name of that place Succoth, that is, taber-nacles.
33.18: And Jacob passed into Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, after that he turned again from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he dwelled beside the city.
33.19: And he bought for an hundred lambs a part of the field, in which he set tabernacles, of the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem.
33.20: And when he had raised an altar there, he inwardly called on it the full strong God of Israel.

34.1: Forsooth Dinah, the daughter of Leah, went out to see the women of that country.
34.2: And when Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of that land, had seen her, he loved her, and he ravished her, and slept with her, and oppressed the virgin by violence.
34.3: And his soul was bound fast with her, and he pleased her sorry with flatterings.
34.4: And he went to Hamor, his father, and said, Take to me this damsel for a wife.
34.5: And when Jacob had heard this thing, while his sons were absent, and occupied in the feeding or the pasturing of [[the]] sheep, he was still, till they came again.
34.6: Soothly when Hamor, the father of Shechem, was gone out to speak to Jacob,
34.7: lo! his sons came from the field. And when this thing that befelled was heard, they were wroth greatly; for he had wrought a foul thing in Israel, and he had done a thing unleaveful in the defouling of the daughter of Jacob.
34.8: And so Hamor spake to them, The soul of my son Shechem hath cleaved to your daughter; give ye her a wife to him,
34.9: and join we weddings together; give ye your daughters to us, and take ye our daughters,
34.10: and dwell ye with us; the land is in your power; till ye, and make ye merchandise, and wield ye it.
34.11: But also Shechem said to the father and brethren of her, Find I grace before you, and whatever things ye ordain I shall give;
34.12: increase ye the dower, and ask ye for gifts, and I shall give willfully that that ye ask; only give ye this damsel a wife to me.
34.13: The sons of Jacob answered in guile to Shechem and to Hamor, his father, and they were made fierce for the defouling of the maidenhood of their sister,
34.14: We may not do this that ye ask, neither we may give our sister to a man uncircumcised, which thing is unleaveful and abominable with us.
34.15: But in this we shall be able to be bound in peace, if ye will be like us, and each of male kind be circumcised in you;
34.16: then we shall give and take together our daughters and yours; and we shall dwell with you, and we shall be one people.
34.17: Forsooth if ye will not be cir-cumcised, we shall take our daughter, and we shall go away.
34.18: The proffering of them pleased Hamor, and Shechem, his son,
34.19: and the young waxing man delayed not, that not he fulfilled anon that that was asked; for he loved the damsel greatly, and he was the most noble in all the house of his father.
34.20: And they entered into the gate of the city, and spake to the people,
34.21: These men be peaceable, and will dwell with us; make they merchandise in the land, and till they it, which is large and broad, and hath need to tillers; we shall take their daughters to wives, and we shall give our daughters to them.
34.22: One thing is, for which so great good is delayed; if we circumcise our males, and follow the custom of the folk,
34.23: both their substance, and sheep, and all things which they wield, shall be ours; only assent we in this, that we dwell together, and make one people.
34.24: And all men assented, and all [[the]] males were circumcised.
34.25: And lo! in the third day, when the sorrow of [[the]] wounds was most grievous, two sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, [[the]] brethren of Dinah, took swords, and entered into the city boldly; and when all [[the]] males were slain,
34.26: they killed Hamor and Shechem together, and took Dinah, their sister, from the house of Shechem. And when they were gone out,
34.27: [[the]] other sons of Jacob felled in on the slain men, and rifled the city, for the vengeance of [[the]] defouling of the virgin.
34.28: And they wasted the sheep of those men, and droves of oxen, and asses, and all things that were in the houses and fields,
34.29: and led away as prisoners the little children, and [[the]] wives of those men. And when these things were done hardily,
34.30: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me, and have made me hateful to Canaanites and Perizzites, [[the]] dwellers of this land; we be few, [[and]] they shall be gathered together against me, and shall slay me, and I shall be done away, and mine house.
34.31: Simeon and Levi answered, Whether they ought to mis-use our sister as a whore?

35.1: In the meantime the Lord spake to Jacob, Rise thou, and go up to Bethel, and dwell there; and make thou an altar to the Lord, that appeared to thee when thou fleddest Esau, thy brother.
35.2: Soothly Jacob said, when all his house was called together, Cast ye away alien gods, that be in the midst of you, and be ye cleansed, and change ye your clothes;
35.3: rise ye, and go we up into Bethel, that we make there an altar to the Lord, which heard me in the day of my tribulation, and was fellow of my way.
35.4: Therefore they gave to Jacob all the alien gods which they had, and [[the]] earrings, that were in their ears; and Jacob delved them under a terebinth tree, which is behind the city of Shechem.
35.5: And when they went forth, dread assailed all men by compass of the city, and they were not hardy to pursue them going away.
35.6: Therefore Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, by the sire-name Bethel, he and all his people with him.
35.7: And he builded there an altar to the Lord, and called the name of that place The house of God, for God appeared there to him, when he fled his brother.
35.8: Deborah, the nurse of Rebecca, died in the same time, and she was buried at the root[[s]] of Bethel, under an oak, and the name of the place was called The Oak of Weeping.
35.9: Forsooth God appeared again to Jacob, after that he turned again from Mesopotamia of Syria, and came into Bethel, and blessed him,
35.10: and said, Thou shalt no more be called Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name. And God called him Israel,
35.11: and said to him, I am God Almighty; increase thou, and be thou multiplied, folks and peoples of nations shall be of thee, kings shall go out of thy loins;
35.12: and I shall give to thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac.
35.14: Forsooth Jacob raised a title, or a memorial, of stones, in the place wherein God spake to him, and he sacrificed thereon flowing sacrifices, and shedded out oil,
35.15: and he called the name of that place Bethel.
35.16: Soothly Jacob went out from thence, and he came in the beginning of summer to the land that leadeth to Ephratah; in which land when Rachel travailed in child bearing,
35.17: she began to be in peril for the hardness of childbearing; and the mid-wife said to her, Do not thou dread, for thou shalt have also this son.
35.18: Forsooth while the soul passed from her for sorrow, and death nighed then, she called the name of her son Benoni, that is, the son of my sorrow; forsooth his father called him Benjamin, that is, the son of the right side.
35.19: Therefore Rachel died, and was buried in the way that leadeth to Ephratah, that is Bethlehem.
35.20: And Jacob builded a memorial upon the sepulchre of her; this is the memorial of the burial of Rachel unto this present day.
35.21: Jacob went from thence, and setted a tabernacle over the tower of the flock.
35.22: And while he dwelled in that country, Reuben went, and slept with Bilhah, the secondary wife of his father, which thing was not hid from him. Forsooth the sons of Jacob were twelve;
35.23: the sons of Leah were, the first begotten Reuben, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun;
35.24: the sons of Rachel were Joseph, and Benjamin;
35.25: the sons of Bilhah, the handmaid of Rachel, were Dan, and Naphtali;
35.26: and the sons of Zilpah, [[the]] handmaid of Leah, were Gad, and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob, that were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.
35.27: Also Jacob came to Isaac, his father, into Mamre, the city of Arbah, this is Hebron, in which Mamre Abraham and Isaac was a pilgrim.
35.28: And the days of Isaac were filled an hundred and fourscore of years;
35.29: and he was wasted in age, and died, and he was put to his people, and was eld [[or old]], and full of days; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.

36.1: Forsooth these be the generations of Esau; he is Edom.
36.2: Esau took wives of the daughters of Canaan; Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the son of Zibeon the Hivite;
36.3: also Bashemath, the daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebajoth.
36.4: And Adah childed Eliphaz; Bashemath childed Reuel;
36.5: Oholibamah childed Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah. These were the sons of Esau, that were born to him in the land of Canaan.
36.6: Soothly Esau took his wives, and his sons, and daughters, and each soul of his house, and his cattle, and sheep, and all things which he had in the land of Canaan, and went into another country, and departed from his brother Jacob;
36.7: for they were full rich, and they might not dwell together, and the land of their pilgrimage sustained not them, for the multitude of flocks.
36.8: And Esau dwelled in the hill of Seir; he is Edom.
36.9: Forsooth these were the genera-tions of Esau, father of Edom, in the hill of Seir,
36.10: and these were the names of his sons; Eliphaz, the son of Adah, wife of Esau, also Reuel, the son of Bashemath, wife of Esau.
36.11: And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
36.12: Forsooth Timna was the secondary wife of Eliphaz, Esau’s son, which Timna childed to him Amalek. These were the sons of Adah, Esau’s wife.
36.13: Forsooth the sons of Reuel were Nahath, and Zerah, and Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Bashemath, Esau’s wife.
36.14: And these were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, son of Zibeon, Esau’s wife, which she childed to him; Jeush, and Jaalam, and Korah.
36.15: These were dukes of the sons of Esau; the sons of Eliphaz, the first engendered of Esau; duke Teman, duke Omar, duke Zepho, duke Kenaz,
36.16: duke Korah, duke Gatam, and duke Amalek. These were the sons of Eliphaz, in the land of Edom, and these were the sons of Adah.
36.17: Also these were the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son; duke Nahath, duke Zerah, duke Shammah, duke Mizzah; forsooth these dukes were of Reuel, in the land of Edom. These were the sons of Bashemath, Esau’s wife.
36.18: Forsooth these were the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife; duke Jeush, duke Jaalam, duke Korah; these were [[the]] dukes of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.
36.19: These were the sons of Esau, and these were dukes of them; he is Edom.
36.20: These were the sons of Seir the Horite, inhabiters of the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,
36.21: and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan; these dukes were of Horites, the son[[s]] of Seir, in the land of Edom.
36.22: Forsooth the sons of Lotan were Hori, and Hemam; soothly the sister of Lotan was Timna.
36.23: And these were the sons of Shobal; Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
36.24: And these were the sons of Zibeon; Ajah, and Anah; this is Ahan that found hot waters in the wilderness, when he kept the asses of Zibeon, his father;
36.25: and he had a son, Dishon, and a daughter, Oholibamah.
36.26: And these were the sons of Dishon; Hemdan, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
36.27: Also these were the sons of Ezer; Bilhan, and Zaavan, and Akan.
36.28: And Dishon had sons; Uz, and Aran.
36.29: These were the dukes of Horites; duke Lotan, duke Shobal, duke Zibeon, duke Anah,
36.30: duke Dishon, duke Ezer, duke Dishan; these were the dukes of Horites, that were lords in the land of Seir.
36.31: Forsooth [[the]] kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before that the sons of Israel had a king, were these;
36.32: Bela, the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
36.33: Forsooth Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, reigned for him.
36.34: And when Jobab was dead, Husham of the land of Temani reigned for him.
36.35: And when he was dead, Hadad, the son of Bedad, that smote Midian in the land of Moab, and the name of his city was Avith, reigned for him.
36.36: And when Hadad was dead, Samlah of Masrekah reigned for him.
36.37: And when he was dead, Saul of the flood [[of]] Rehoboth reigned for him.
36.38: And when he was dead, Baal-hanan, the son of Achbor, was successor into the realm.
36.39: And when he was dead, Hadar reigned for him, and the name of the city of Hadar was Pau, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
36.40: Therefore these were the names of the dukes of Esau, in their kindreds, and places, and names; duke Timnah, duke Alvah, duke Jetheth,
36.41: duke Oholibamah, duke Elah, duke Pinon,
36.42: duke Kenaz, duke Teman, duke Mibzar,
36.43: duke Magdiel, duke Iram; these were the dukes of Edom, dwelling in the land of his lordship; he was Esau, the father of Idumeans.

37.1: Forsooth Jacob dwelled in the land of Canaan, in which his father was a pilgrim;
37.2: and these were the generations of him. Joseph when he was of sixteen years, yet a child, kept a flock with his brethren, and he was with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, the wives of his father; and he accused his brethren at the father of the worst sin.
37.3: Forsooth Israel loved Joseph above all his sons, for he had begotten him in his eld age; and he made to Joseph a coat of many colours.
37.4: Forsooth his brethren saw that he was loved of the father more than all they, and they hated him, and might not speak anything peaceably to him.
37.5: And it befelled that he told to his brethren a sweven that he saw, which cause was the seed of more hatred.
37.6: And Joseph said to his brethren, Hear ye the sweven which I saw,
37.7: I guessed that we bound together sheaves, or handfuls, [[in the field]], and that as mine handful rose up, and stood upright, and that your handfuls stood about, and worshipped or honoured mine handful.
37.8: His brethren answered, Whether thou shalt be our king, either we shall be made subject to thy lordship? Therefore this cause of dreams and words ministered the nourishing of envy, and of hatred.
37.9: Also Joseph saw another sweven, which he told to his brethren, and said, I saw a dream that as the sun, and the moon, and the eleven stars worshipped me.
37.10: And when he had told this dream to his father, and his brethren, his father blamed him, and said, What will this dream mean to itself that thou hast seen? Whether I, and thy mother, and thy brethren, shall worship thee on earth?
37.11: Therefore his brethren had envy to him. Forsooth the father beheld privily the thing,
37.12: and when his brethren dwelled in Shechem, about [[the]] keeping of [[the]] flocks of their father,
37.13: Israel said to Joseph, Thy brethren keep sheep in Shechem; come thou, I shall send thee to them. And when Joseph answered, I am ready,
37.14: Israel said, Go thou, and see whether all things be welsome with thy brethren, and the sheep; and then tell thou to me what is done. And so he was sent from the valley of Hebron, and came into Shechem;
37.15: and a man found him erring in the field, and the man asked him, what he sought.
37.16: And he answered, I seek my brethren; show thou to me where they keep their flocks.
37.17: And the man said to him, They went away from this place; forsooth I heard them saying, Go we into Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothan.
37.18: And when they had seen him afar, before he nighed to them, they thought to slay him,
37.19: and they spake together, Lo! the dreamer cometh,
37.20: come ye, slay we him, and put we him into an eld [[or old]] cistern, and we shall say, A wild beast full wicked hath devoured him; and then it shall appear what his dreams profit to him.
37.21: Soothly Reuben heard this, and enforced or endeavoured to deliver him from their hands, and said, Slay we not the life of him,
37.22: neither shed we out his blood, but cast ye him into an eld [[or old]] cistern, which is in the wilderness, and keep ye your hands guiltless. Forsooth he said this, willing to deliver him from their hands, and to yield him to his father.
37.23: Therefore anon as Joseph came to his brethren, they despoiled him of his coat, that went down to the heel, and was of many colours,
37.24: and they put him in[[to]] an eld [[or old]] cistern, that had no water.
37.25: And they sat to eat bread; and they saw that Ishmaelite way-goers came from Gilead, and that their camels bare sweet smelling spiceries, and resin, and stacte, into Egypt.
37.26: Therefore Judah said to his brethren, What shall it profit to us, if we shall slay our brother, and shall hide his blood?
37.27: It is better that he be sold to Ishmaelites, and our hands be not defouled, for he is our brother and our flesh. His brethren assented to these words;
37.28: and when [[the]] merchants of Midian passed thereforth, they drew Joseph out of the cistern, and sold him to Ishmaelites, for twenty pieces of silver; which led him into Egypt.
37.29: And Reuben turned again to the cistern, and found not the child; and he rent his clothes,
37.30: and he went to his brethren, and said, The child appeareth not, and whither shall I go?
37.31: Forsooth they took his coat, and dipped it in the blood of a kid, which they had slain;
37.32: and they sent men that bare it to their father, and said, We have found this coat; see thou, whether it is the coat of thy son, or nay.
37.33: And when their father had known it, he said, It is the coat of my son; a wild beast full wicked hath eaten him; a beast hath devoured Joseph.
37.34: And he rent his clothes, and he was clothed with an hair-shirt, and bewailed his son in much time.
37.35: Soothly when his free children were gathered together, that they should appease the sorrow of their father, he would not take comfort; but said, I shall go down into hell, and shall bewail my son. And while Jacob continued in weeping,
37.36: Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, a chaste and honest servant [[or the gelding]] of Pharaoh, master of the chivalry.

38.1: In the same time, Judah went down from his brethren, and turned to a man of Adullam, Hirah by name;
38.2: and he saw there a daughter of a man of Canaan, Shuah by name. And when he had taken her to wife, he entered [[in]] to her,
38.3: and she conceived, and childed a son, and he called his name Er.
38.4: And again when another child was conceived, she named the child that was born Onan.
38.5: And she childed the third son, whom she called Shelah, and when he was born, she ceased to bear child more.
38.6: Soothly Judah gave a wife, that was called Tamar, to his first begotten son Er.
38.7: And Er, the first begotten son of Judah, was wayward in the sight of the Lord, and therefore he was slain of the Lord.
38.8: Therefore Judah said to Onan, his son, Enter thou [[in]] to the wife of thy brother, and be thou fellowshipped to her, that thou raise seed to thy brother.
38.9: And he knew that sons should not be born to him; and he entered [[in]] to the wife of his brother, and shedded his seed into the earth, lest the free children should be born by the name of the dead brother;
38.10: and therefore the Lord smote him, for he did abominable thing.
38.11: Wherefore Judah said to Tamar, his son’s wife, Be thou a widow in the house of thy father, till Shelah my son waxed; for he dreaded lest also he should die as his brethren. And she went, and dwelled in the house of her father.
38.12: Forsooth when many years were passed, the daughter of Shuah, Judah’s wife, died; and when comfort was taken after mourning, Judah went up to the shearers of his sheep; he and Hirah of Adullam, that was [[the]] keeper of the flock, went up into Timnath.
38.13: And it was told to Tamar, that her husband’s father went up into Timnath, to shear sheep.
38.14: And she did away the clothes of widowhood, and she took a rochet cloth or veil with many wrinkles, and when the clothing was changed, she sat in the way-lot that leadeth to Timnath; for Shelah had waxed, and she had not taken him into husband.
38.15: And when Judah had seen her, he supposed her to be a whore; for she had covered her face, lest she was known.
38.16: And Judah entered to her, and said, Suffer me that I lie with thee; for he knew not that she was the wife of his son. And when she answered, What shalt thou give to me, that thou lie with me?
38.17: he said, I shall send to thee a kid of the flocks. And again when she said, I shall suffer that that thou wilt, if thou shalt give to me a wed, till thou send that that thou promisest.
38.18: Judah said, What wilt thou that be given to thee for a wed? She answered, Thy ring, and thy band of the arm, and the staff which thou holdest in thine hand. Therefore the woman conceived at one lying-by,
38.19: and she rose, and went [[away]]; and when the cloth or veil was put away which she had taken, she was clothed in the clothes of widowhood.
38.20: Forsooth Judah sent a kid by his shepherd of Adullam, that he should receive the wed which he had given to the woman; and when he had not found her,
38.21: he asked men of that place, Where is the woman that sat in the way-lot? And when all men answered, A whore was not in this place;
38.22: he turned again to Judah, and said to him, I found not her, but also the men of that place said to me, that a whore sat never there.
38.23: Judah said, Have she those things to herself, that we be not despised, certainly she may not reprove us of a leasing; I sent the kid which I promised, and thou foundest not her.
38.24: Lo! soothly after three months they told to Judah, and said, Tamar, thy son’s wife, hath done fornication, and her womb seemeth to wax great. Judah said, Bring her forth, that she be burnt.
38.25: And when she was led to her pain, she sent to her husband’s father, and said, I have conceived of the man, whose these things be; know thou whose is the ring, and the band of the arm, and the staff?
38.26: And when the gifts were known, Judah said, She is more just [[or rightwise]] than I, for I gave not her to Shelah, my son; nevertheless Judah knew her no more fleshly.
38.27: Soothly when the childbearing nighed, two children appeared in the womb,
38.28: and in that birth of the children, one put forth the hand, in which hand the midwife bound a red thread, and said, This shall go out before.
38.29: Soothly while he withdrew the hand, the tother went out, and the woman said, Why, was the skin in which the child lay in the womb parted for thee? And for this cause she called his name Perez.
38.30: Afterward his brother went out, in whose hand was the red thread, whom she called Zarah, that is, Redness.

39.1: Therefore Joseph was led into Egypt, and Potiphar, a gelding of Pharaoh, prince of the host, a man of Egypt, bought him of the hand of Ishmaelites, of which he was brought thither.
39.2: And the Lord was with him, and he was a man doing with prosperity in all things. And Joseph dwelled in the house of his lord,
39.3: which knew full well that the Lord was with Joseph, and that all things which he did, were dressed of the Lord in his hand.
39.4: And Joseph found grace before his lord, and he served him, of whom Joseph was made sovereign of all things, and he governed the house betaken to him, and all things that were betaken to him.
39.5: And the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph, and multiplied all his chattel [[or substance]], as well in houses, as in fields;
39.6: neither he knew any other thing, but [[the]] bread which he ate. Forsooth Joseph was fair in face, and shapely in sight.
39.7: And so after many days the lady of his lord cast her eyes into Joseph, and said, Sleep thou with me;
39.8: which assented not to the unleave-ful work, and said to her, Lo! while all things be betaken to me, my lord wot not what he hath in his house,
39.9: neither anything is, which is not in my power, either which he hath not betaken to me, except thee, which art his wife; how therefore may I do this evil, and do sin against my lord?
39.10: They spake such words by all days or by long time, and the woman was dis-easeful to the young man, and he forsook the adultery.
39.11: Forsooth it befelled in a day, that Joseph entered into the house, and did some work without witnesses.
39.12: And she took the hem of his cloth, and she said, Sleep thou with me; and he left the mantle in her hand, and he fled, and went out.
39.13: And when the woman had seen the cloth in her hands, and that she was despised,
39.14: she called to her the men of her house, and said to them, Lo! my lord hath brought in an Hebrew man, that he should scorn us; he entered to me to do lechery with me, and when I cried,
39.15: and he heard my voice, he left the mantle which I held, and he fled out.
39.16: Therefore into proving of the truth, she showed the mantle, that she held, to her husband turning again home.
39.17: And she said, The Hebrew servant, whom thou broughtest in, entered to me to scorn me;
39.18: and when he saw me cry, he left the mantle that I held, and he fled out.
39.19: And when these things were heard, the lord believed over much to the words of the wife, and he was full wroth;
39.20: and he betook Joseph into prison, where the bound men of the king were kept, and he was enclosed there.
39.21: Forsooth the Lord was with Joseph, and had mercy on him, and gave grace to him, in the sight of the prince of the prison,
39.22: which betook in the hand of Joseph all the prisoners that were holden in keeping, and whatever thing was done, it was done under Joseph,
39.23: neither the prince knew anything, for all things were betaken to Joseph; for the Lord was with him, and dressed all his works.

40.1: When these things were done, it befelled that two geldings, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, sinned to their lord.
40.2: And Pharaoh was wroth against them, for the one was master butler, and the tother was master baker.
40.3: And he sent them into the prison of the prince of knights, in which also Joseph was bound.
