40.4: And the keeper of the prison betook them to Joseph, which also served, or kept, them. Somewhat of time passed, and they were holden in keeping,
40.5: and both saw a dream in one night, by covenable expounding to them.
40.6: And when Joseph had entered to them early, and had seen them sorry,
40.7: he asked them, and said, Why is your cheer heavier today than it is wont to be?
40.8: Which answered, We each saw a dream, and there is no man that expoundeth it to us. And Joseph said to them, Whether the expounding is not of God? Tell ye to me what ye have seen.
40.9: The master butler told first his dream; I saw before me that a vine,
40.10: in which were three scions, waxed little and little into burgeonings, and that after the flowers, the grapes waxed ripe,
40.11: and the cup of Pharaoh was in mine hand; therefore I took the grapes, and pressed them out into the cup that I held, and I gave drink to Pharaoh.
40.12: Joseph answered, This is the expounding of the dream; three scions be yet three days,
40.13: after which Pharaoh shall have mind of thy service, and he shall restore thee into the first degree, and thou shalt give to him the cup, by thine office, as thou were wont to do before.
40.14: Only have thou mind of me, when it is well to thee, and thou shalt do mercy with me, that thou make suggestion to Pharaoh, that he lead me out of this prison;
40.15: for thiefly, that is, by thievery, I am taken away from the land of Hebrews, and here I am sent innocent into prison.
40.16: The master baker saw that Joseph had declared prudently the dream, and he said, And I saw a dream, that I had three baskets of meal on mine head,
40.17: and I guessed that I bare in one basket, that was highest, all meats or baked foods that be made for Pharaoh by the craft of bakers, and that birds ate thereof.
40.18: Joseph answered, This is the expounding of the dream; three baskets be yet three days,
40.19: after which Pharaoh shall take away thine head, and he shall hang thee in a cross, and birds shall draw thy flesh.
40.20: From thence the third day was the day of the birth of Pharaoh, which made a great feast to his servants, and he had mind among the meats or during the meal, of the master butler, and of the prince of bakers;
40.21: and he restored the one into his place, that he should dress the cup, either drink, to the king,
40.22: and he hanged the tother in a gibbet, that the truth of Joseph declaring the dreams should be proved.
40.23: And nevertheless when prosperities befelled to the master butler, he forgat Joseph that declared his dream.

41.1: After two years Pharaoh saw a dream; he guessed that he stood on a river,
41.2: from which seven fair kine and full fat went up, and [[they]] were fed in the places of marshes;
41.3: and another seven, foul and lean, came out of the river, and were fed in that brink of the water, in green places;
41.4: and those foul and lean kine devoured those kine of which the fairness and comeliness of their bodies were wonderful. Pharaoh waked,
41.5: and slept again, and he saw another dream; seven ears of corn, full and fair, came forth in one stalk,
41.6: and others, as many ears of corn, thin and smitten with corruption of burning wind, came forth,
41.7: devouring all the fairness of the first. Pharaoh waked after this rest,
41.8: and when the morrowtide was made, he was afeared by inward dread, and he sent to all the expounders of Egypt, and to all the wise men; and when they were called, he told the dream, and none was that expounded it.
41.9: Then at the last, the master butler bethought to him, and said to Pharaoh, I acknowledge my sin;
41.10: the king was wroth to his servants, and commanded me and the master baker to be cast down into the prison of the prince of knights,
41.11: where we both saw a dream in one night, before-showing of things to come.
41.12: An Hebrew child, servant of the same duke of knights, was there, to whom we told the dreams, and heard whatever thing the befalling of [[the]] thing proved afterward;
41.13: for I am restored to mine office, and he was hanged in a cross.
41.14: Anon at the behest of the king, they polled Joseph, led him out of the prison, and when his clothing was changed, they brought him to the king.
41.15: To whom the king said, I saw dreams, and none [[there]] is that expoundeth those things that I saw; I have heard that thou expoundest such things most prudently.
41.16: Joseph answered, Without me, God shall answer prosperities to Pharaoh.
41.17: Therefore Pharaoh told that that he saw; I guessed that I stood on the brink of the flood,
41.18: and seven kine, full fair, with flesh able to eating, went up from the water, which kine gathered green sedges in the pasture of the marshes;
41.19: and lo! seven other kine, so foul and lean, followed these, that I saw never such in the land of Egypt;
41.20: and when the former kine were devoured and wasted of the lean kine,
41.21: the lean kine gave no step, or token, of fullness, but were slow, or feeble, by like leanness and paleness. I waked,
41.22: and again I was oppressed by sleep, and I saw a dream; seven ears of corn, full and most fair, came forth on one stalk,
41.23: and another seven, thin and smitten with [[a]] burning wind, came forth of the stubble,
41.24: which devoured the fairness of the former; I told this dream to [[the]] expounders, and no man there is that expoundeth it.
41.25: Joseph answered, The dream of the king is one; God hath showed to Pharaoh what things he shall do.
41.26: Seven fair kine, and seven full ears of corn, be seven years of plenty, and the same things comprehend the strength of the dream;
41.27: and [[the]] seven kine, thin and lean, that went up after the fair kine, and the seven thin ears of corn, and smitten with [[a]] burning wind, be seven years of hunger to coming [[or to come]],
41.28: which shall be fulfilled by this order.
41.29: Lo! seven years of great plenty in all the land of Egypt shall come,
41.30: and seven other years of so great barrenness shall pursue [[or follow]] those, that all the abundance before shall be given to forgetting; for hunger shall waste all the land,
41.31: and the greatness of neediness shall waste the greatness of plenty.
41.32: Forsooth this that thou sawest the second time in a dream pertaining to the same thing, is a showing of firm-ness, that is, a confirming of the first, for the word of God shall be done, and it shall be [[ful]] filled full swiftly.
41.33: Now therefore purvey the king a wise man and a ready, and make the king him sovereign to the land of Egypt,
41.34: which man ordain governors by all countries, and gather he into barns the fifth part of fruits by [[the]] seven years of plenty, that shall come now;
41.35: and all the wheat be kept under the power of Pharaoh, and be it kept in [[the]] cities,
41.36: and be it made ready to the hunger to coming [[or to come]] of the seven years that shall oppress Egypt, and the land be not wasted by poverty.
41.37: The counsel of Joseph pleased Pharaoh, and all his servants,
41.38: and he spake to them, Whether we be able to find such a man which is full of God’s spirit?
41.39: Therefore Pharaoh said to Joseph, For God hath showed to thee all things which thou hast spoken, whether I may find a wiser man than thou, and like to thee?
41.40: Therefore thou shalt be over mine house, and all the people shall obey to the behest of thy mouth; I shall pass thee only by one throne of the realm.
41.41: And again Pharaoh said to Joseph, Lo! I have ordained thee on all the land of Egypt.
41.42: And Pharaoh took off the ring from his hand, and gave it in the hand of Joseph, and he clothed Joseph with a stole of bis, or of white silk, and he put a golden wreath about his neck;
41.43: and Pharaoh made Joseph to go upon his second chariot, while a beadle cried, that all men should kneel before him, and should know that he was sovereign of all the land of Egypt.
41.44: And the king said to Joseph, I am Pharaoh, without thy behest no man shall stir hand either foot in all the land of Egypt.
41.45: And Pharaoh turned the name of Joseph, and called him by the Egyptian language, The Saviour of the World, or Zaphnathpaaneah; and he gave to Joseph a wife, Asenath, the daughter of Potipherah, a priest of Heliopolis, that is, The City of the Sun. And so Joseph went out to the land of Egypt.
41.46: Forsooth Joseph was of thirty years, when he stood in the sight of king Pharaoh, and compassed all the countries [[or regions]] of Egypt.
41.47: And the plenty of [[the]] seven years came, and [[the]] ripe corns were bound into handfuls or sheaves,
41.48: and they were gathered into the barns of Egypt, also all the abundance of ripe corns was kept in all cities,
41.49: and so great abundance was of wheat, that it was made even to the gravel, or the sand, of the sea, and the plenty passed measure.
41.50: Soothly two sons were born to Joseph before that the hunger came, which Asenath, the daughter of Potipherah, a priest of Heliopolis, childed to him.
41.51: And Joseph called the name of the first begotten son, Manasseh, and said, God hath made me to forget all my travails, and the house of my father;
41.52: and he called the name of the second son Ephraim, and said, God hath made me to increase in the land of my poverty.
41.53: Therefore when seven years of plenty that were in Egypt were passed,
41.54: [[the]] seven years of poverty began to come, which Joseph before-said, and hunger had the mastery in all the world; also hunger was in all the land of Egypt;
41.55: and when that land hungered, the people cried to Pharaoh, and asked for meats; to whom he answered, Go ye to Joseph, and do ye whatever thing he saith to you.
41.56: Forsooth hunger increased each day in all the land, and Joseph opened all the barns, and sold corn to the Egyptians, for also hunger oppressed them;
41.57: and all [[the]] provinces came into Egypt to buy corns, and to abate the evil of neediness.

42.1: Forsooth Jacob heard that foods were sold in Egypt, and he said to his sons, Why be ye negligent?
42.2: I [[have]] heard that wheat is sold in Egypt; go ye down, and buy ye necessaries to us, that we may live, and be not wasted by neediness.
42.3: Therefore ten brethren of Joseph went down to buy wheat in Egypt,
42.4: and Benjamin was withholden of Jacob at home, that said to his brethren, Lest peradventure in the way he suffer any evil.
42.5: Soothly they entered into the land of Egypt, with other men that went thither to buy corn; forsooth hunger was in the land of Canaan.
42.6: And Joseph was the prince of Egypt, and at his will wheats were sold to [[the]] peoples. And when his brethren had worshipped or honoured him,
42.7: and he had known them, he spake harder to them, as to aliens, and asked them, From whence came ye? Which answered, From the land of Canaan, that we buy necessaries to our lifelode.
42.8: And nevertheless he knew his brethren, and he was not known of them,
42.9: and he bethought on the dreams which he saw sometime. And he said to them, Ye be spyers [[or spies]], ye came to see the feebler things of the land.
42.10: Which said, Lord, it is not so, but thy servants came to buy meats;
42.11: all we be [[the]] sons of one man, we came hither peaceably, and thy servants imagine not any evil.
42.12: To which he answered, It is in other manner, ye came to see the feeble things of the land.
42.13: And they said, We thy servants be twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; the youngest is with our father, another is not alive.
42.14: This it is, he said, that I spake to you, ye be spyers [[or spies]],
42.15: right now I shall take experience or very knowing of you; by the health of Pharaoh ye shall not go from hence, till your least brother come hither;
42.16: send ye one of you, that he bring him, forsooth ye shall be in bonds till those things that ye said be proved, whether those [[or they]] be false or true; else, by the health of Pharaoh, ye be spies.
42.17: Therefore he betook them into keeping three days;
42.18: soothly in the third day, when they were led out of prison, Joseph said, Do ye that that I said, and ye shall live, for I dread God;
42.19: if ye be peaceable, one brother of you be bound in prison; forsooth the rest go ye, and bear the wheat, which ye have bought, into your houses,
42.20: and bring ye your youngest brother to me, that I may prove your words, and ye die not. They did as he said,
42.21: and they spake together, Worthily we suffer these things, for we sinned against our brother, and we saw the anguish of his soul, while he prayed us, and we heard him not; therefore this tribulation cometh on us.
42.22: Of which one, Reuben, said, Whether I said not to you, Do not ye sin against the child, and ye heard not me? lo! his blood is sought.
42.23: Soothly they knew not that Joseph understood them, for he spake to them by an interpreter or an expounder.
42.24: And he turned away himself a little, and wept; and he turned again, and spake to them. And he took Simeon, and bound him, while they were present;
42.25: and he commanded the servants, that they should fill their sacks with wheat, and that they should put all their money in their bags, and over this give to them meats in the way; which did so.
42.26: And they bare [[the]] wheats on their asses, and went forth,
42.27: and when the sack of one of them was opened that he should give meat to the work beast in the inn, he beheld the money in the mouth of the bag,
42.28: and he said to his brethren, My money is yielded to me, lo! it is had in the bag; and they were astonied, and troubled, and said together, What thing is this that God hath done to us?
42.29: And they came to Jacob, their father, in the land of Canaan, and told to him all things that befelled to them, and said,
42.30: The lord of the land spake hard to us, and guessed that we were spyers [[or spies]] of the province;
42.31: to whom we answered, We be peaceable, neither we purpose any treasons;
42.32: we be twelve brethren, engendered of one father, one is not alive, the youngest dwelleth with the father in the land of Canaan.
42.33: And he said to us, Thus I shall prove that ye be peaceable; leave ye one brother of you with me, and take ye meats needful to your houses, and go ye,
42.34: and bring ye to me your youngest brother, that I know that ye be not spyers [[or spies]], and that ye may receive this brother which is holden in bonds, and that from thenceforth ye have license to buy what things ye will.
42.35: While these things were said, when they all poured out the wheats, they found the money bound in the mouths of their sacks. And when they altogether were afeared,
42.36: their father Jacob said, Ye have made me to be without children; Joseph is not alive, Simeon is holden in bonds, ye shall take away from me Benjamin; all these evils have fallen in on me.
42.37: To whom Reuben answered, Slay thou my two sons, if I shall not bring him again to thee; take thou him in mine hand, and I shall restore him to thee.
42.38: And Jacob said, My son shall not go down with you; his brother is dead, he alone is left; if any adversity shall befall to him in the land to which ye shall go, ye shall lead forth mine hoar hairs with sorrow to hell.

43.1: In the meantime hunger oppressed greatly all the land,
43.2: and when the meats were wasted or consumed, which they [[had]] brought from Egypt, Jacob said to his sons, Turn ye again, and buy ye a little of meats to us.
43.3: Judah answered, That man announced to us, under witnessing of an oath, and said, Ye shall not see my face, if ye shall not bring with you your least brother;
43.4: therefore if thou wilt send him with us, we shall go down together, and we shall buy necessaries to thee;
43.5: else if thou wilt not, we shall not go down; for as we said oft, the man announced to us, and said, Ye shall not see my face without your least brother.
43.6: Forsooth Israel said to them, Ye did this into my wretchedness, that ye showed to him, that ye had also another brother.
43.7: And they answered, The man asked us by order our generation, if our father lived, if we had another brother; and we answered pursuingly to him, by that that he asked; whether we might know that he would say, Bring ye your brother with you?
43.8: And Judah said to his father, Send the child with me, that we go, and may live, lest we die, and thou, and our little children;
43.9: I shall take the child, require thou him again of mine hand; if I shall not bring him again, and betake him to thee, I shall be guilty of sin against thee in all time;
43.10: if this delay, or tarrying, had not been, we had come thence now another time.
43.11: Therefore Israel, their father, said to them, If it is need so to be, do ye that that ye will; take ye of the best fruits of the land in your vessels, and bear ye gifts to the man, a little of gum, and of honey, and of storax, that is, a precious gum, and of myrrh, that is, a bitter gum, and of terebinth, that is, best resins, and of almonds;
43.12: and bear ye with you double money, and bear ye again that money which ye found in [[the]] bags, lest peradventure it be done by error, or unwittingly, or by negligence;
43.13: but also take ye your brother, and go ye to the man;
43.14: forsooth my God Almighty make him peaceable or pleasable, or queme-ful, to you, and send he again your brother, whom he holdeth in bonds, and also this Benjamin; forsooth I shall be now as made bare without sons.
43.15: Therefore the men took gifts, and double money, and Benjamin; and they went down into Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
43.16: And when he had seen them and Benjamin together, he commanded the dispenser of his house, and said, Lead these men into the house, and slay some beasts, and make a feast; for they shall eat with me today.
43.17: He did as it was commanded or as it was bidden to him, and he led the men into the house;
43.18: and there they were afeared, and they said together, We be brought in for the money which we bare again before in our sacks, that he put challenge against us, and make subject by violence to servage both us and our asses.
43.19: Wherefore they nighed in the gates, and spake to the dispenser,
43.20: Lord, we pray, that thou hear us; we came down now before that we should buy meats;
43.21: when those were bought, and we headed home, when we came to the inn, we opened our bags, and we found the money in the mouths of our sacks, which money we have brought again now in the same weight;
43.22: but also we have brought other silver, that we can buy those things that be needful to us; it is not in our knowing who put the money in our purses.
43.23: And he answered, Peace be to you, do not ye dread; your God, and [[the]] God of your father, gave to you treasures in your bags; for I have the money proved, which ye gave to me. And he led out Simeon to them;
43.24: and when they were brought into the house, he brought water, and they washed their feet, and he gave their asses meats.
43.25: Soothly they made ready their gifts till Joseph entered at midday, for they had heard that they should eat bread there.
43.26: Therefore Joseph entered into his house, and they offered gifts to him, and held them in their hands, and worshipped low to the earth.
43.27: And he greeted them again meekly; and he asked them, and said, Whether your father, the eld [[or old]] man, is safe, of whom ye said to me? liveth he yet?
43.28: Which answered, He is whole, thy servant our father liveth yet; and they were bowed, and worshipped him.
43.29: Forsooth Joseph raised [[up]] his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother of the same womb, and he said, Is this your youngest brother, of whom ye said to me? And again Joseph said, My son, God have mercy on thee.
43.30: And Joseph hasted into another part of the house, for his entrails were moved on his brother, and tears burst out, and he entered into a closet, and wept.
43.31: And again when his face was washed, he went out, and refrained himself from weeping, and said, Set ye forth loaves.
43.32: Which were set forth to Joseph by himself, and to his brethren by themselves, and to the Egyptians that ate together by themselves; for it is unleaveful to Egyptians to eat with Hebrews, and they guess such a feast unholy.
43.33: Therefore they sat before him, the first begotten by right of the first begotten, and so on down to the youngest by his age; and they wondered greatly,
43.34: when the parts were taken which they had received of him, and the more part came to Benjamin, so that it passed the others in five parts; and they drank, and were [[ful]] filled with him.

44.1: Forsooth Joseph commanded the dispenser of his house, and said, Fill thou their sacks with wheat, as much as they may take, and put thou the money of each in the height [[or the top]] of the sack;
44.2: forsooth put thou in the sack’s mouth of the youngest my silver cup, and the price of the wheat which he gave; and it was done so.
44.3: And when the morrowtide arose, they were delivered with their asses.
44.4: And now they had gone out of the city, and had gone forth a little; then Joseph said, when the dispenser of his house was called, Rise thou, pursue the men, and say thou when they be taken, Why have ye yielded evil for good?
44.5: The cup, which ye have stolen, is that in which my lord drinketh, and in which he is wont to divine; ye have done a full wicked thing.
44.6: He did as Joseph commanded, and when they were overtaken, he spake by order these things;
44.7: the which answered, Why speaketh our lord so, that thy servants have done so great a trespass?
44.8: We brought again to thee from the land of Canaan the money that we found in the height [[or the top]] of our sacks, and how is it pursuing [[or following]] that we have stolen from thy lord’s house gold or silver?
44.9: At whomever of thy servants this that thou seekest is found, die he, and we shall be servants of my lord.
44.10: Which said to them, Be it done by your sentence; at whom it is found, be he my servant; forsooth ye shall be guiltless.
44.11: And so they did down hastily their sacks on the earth, and all they opened them,
44.12: the which he sought through; and he began at the most till to the least, and he found the cup in Benjamin’s sack.
44.13: And when they had rent their clothes, and had charged again their asses, they turned again into the city.
44.14: And Judah entered with his brethren to Joseph; for Joseph had not gone yet from the place; and all they fell together on the earth before him.
44.15: To whom he said, Why would ye do so? whether ye wot not, that none is like me in the knowing of divining?
44.16: To whom Judah said, What shall we answer to my lord, or what shall we speak, either what may we justly against-say? God hath found the wickedness of thy servants; lo! all we be the servants of my lord, both we and he at whom the cup is found.
44.17: Joseph answered, Far be it from me, that I do so; he be my servant that stole the cup; forsooth go ye free to your father.
44.18: Soothly Judah nighed near, and said trustily, My lord, I pray thee, thy servant speak a word in thine ears, and be thou not wroth to thy servant; for after Pharaoh thou art my lord.
44.19: Thou askedest first thy servants, Have ye a father, or a brother?
44.20: And we answered to my lord, An eld [[or old]] father is to us, and a little child that was born in his eld age, whose brother of the same womb is dead, and his mother hath him alone; forsooth his father loveth him tenderly.
44.21: And thou saidest to thy servants, Bring ye him to me, and I shall set mine eyes on him.
44.22: We made suggestion to thee, my lord, the child may not forsake his father; for if he shall leave his father, his father shall die.
44.23: And thou saidest to thy servants, If your youngest brother shall not come down with you, ye shall no more see my face.
44.24: Therefore when we had gone up to thy servant, our father, we told to him all things which my lord spake to us;
44.25: and our father said, Turn ye again, and buy ye to you a little of wheat;
44.26: to whom we said, We may not go; only if our least brother shall go down with us, we shall go forth together; else, if he is absent, we dare not see the lord’s face.
44.27: To which things our father answered, Ye know that my wife childed two sons to me;
44.28: one went out, and ye said, A beast [[hath]] devoured him, and hither-to he appeareth not;
44.29: if ye take also this son, and anything befall to him in the way, ye shall lead forth mine hoar hairs with mourning to hells [[or to hell]].
44.30: Therefore if I enter again to thy servant, our father, and the child fail to be with us, since his life hangeth of the life of the child,
44.31: and he see that the child is not with us, he shall die, and thy servants shall lead forth his hoar hairs with sorrow to hells [[or to hell]].
44.32: Be I properly thy servant, which received this child on my faith, and I promised, and said, If I shall not bring again him to thee, I shall be guilty of sin against my father in all time;
44.33: and so I shall dwell thy servant for the child into the service of my lord, and the child go up with his brethren;
44.34: for I may not go again to my father, if the child be absent, lest I stand a witness of the wretchedness that shall oppress my father.

45.1: Joseph might no longer abstain himself, while many men stood there before him; wherefore he commanded that all men should go out, and that none alien were present in the knowing of Joseph and his brethren.
45.2: And Joseph raised up his voice with weeping, which the Egyptians heard, and all the household of Pharaoh.
45.3: And he said to his brethren, I am Joseph; liveth my father yet? His brethren might not answer, and were aghast with full much dread.
45.4: To whom Joseph said meekly, Cometh nigh to me. And when they had nighed nigh, he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt;
45.5: do not ye dread, neither seem it to be hard to you, that ye sold me into these countries; for God hath sent me before you into Egypt for your health.
45.6: For it is two years that hunger began to be in the land, yet five more years shall pursue, in which men shall not be able to ear, neither reap;
45.7: and God before-sent me, that ye be kept alive on earth, and may have meats to live.
45.8: I was sent hither not by your counsel, but by God’s will, which hath made me as the father of Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and prince in all the land of Egypt.
45.9: Haste ye, and goeth up to my father, and ye shall say to him, Thy son Joseph sendeth these things to thee; God hath made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down here to me, and tarry not,
45.10: and dwell in the land of Goshen; and thou shalt be beside me, thou, and thy sons, and the sons of thy sons, thy sheep, and thy great beasts, and all things which thou wieldest,
45.11: and there I shall feed thee; for yet five years of hunger be left, lest both thou perish, and thine house, and all things which thou wieldest.
45.12: Lo! your eyes, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that my mouth speaketh to you;
45.13: tell ye to my father all my glory, and all things which ye saw in Egypt; haste ye, and bring ye him to me.
45.14: And when he had embraced, and felled into the neck of Benjamin, his brother, he wept, the while also Benjamin wept in like manner on the neck of Joseph.
45.15: And Joseph kissed all his brethren, and wept on them all; after which things they were hardy to speak to him.
45.16: And it was heard, and published by famous word in the king’s hall, The brethren of Joseph be come. And Pharaoh joyed, and all his household;
45.17: and Pharaoh said to Joseph, that he should command his brethren, and say to them, Charge ye your beasts, and go ye into the land of Canaan,
45.18: and take ye from thence your father, and your kindred, and come ye back to me; and I shall give you all the goods of Egypt, that ye eat the marrow of the land.
45.19: Command thou also, that they take wains of the land of Egypt to the carriage of their little children, and wives, and say thou, Take ye your father, and haste ye in coming soon,
45.20: neither leave ye anything of the appurtenance of your house, for all the riches of Egypt shall be yours.
45.21: The sons of Israel did as it was commanded to them; to which Joseph gave wains, by the behest of Pharaoh, and meats in the way;
45.22: and he commanded two stoles to be brought forth to each; forsooth he gave to Benjamin three hundred pieces of silver, with five of the best stoles;
45.23: and he sent to his father so much of silver, and of clothes, and he added to them ten male asses, that should bear of the riches of Egypt, and so many female asses, bearing wheat and loaves in the way.
45.24: Therefore he let go his brethren, and said to them going forth, Be ye not wroth in the way.
45.25: Which went up from Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob;
45.26: and they told to him, and said, Joseph, thy son, liveth, and he is lord in all the land of Egypt. And when this was heard, Jacob waked as of a grievous sleep; nevertheless he believed not to them.
45.27: They told on the contrary to him all the order of the thing; and when Jacob had seen the wains, and all things which Joseph had sent, his spirit lived again,
45.28: and he said, It sufficeth to me, if Joseph my son liveth yet; I shall go and see him before that I die.

46.1: And Israel went forth with all things that he had, and he came to the well of oath or Beersheba; and when sacrifices were slain there to [[the]] God of his father Isaac,
46.2: he heard God by a vision in that night calling to him, and saying to him, Jacob! Jacob! To whom he answered, Lo! I am present.
46.3: God said to him, I am the full strong God of thy father; do not thou dread, go down into Egypt, for I shall make thee there into a great folk;
46.4: I shall go down thither with thee, and I shall bring thee turning again from thence, and Joseph shall set his hand on thine eyes.
46.5: Jacob rose from the well of oath, and his sons took him, with their little children, and wives, in the wains which Pharaoh had sent to bear the eld [[or old]] man,
46.6: and all things which he wielded in the land of Canaan; and he came into Egypt with [[all]] his seed,
46.7: his sons, and their sons, and daughters, and all the generations together.
46.8: Forsooth these be the names of the sons of Israel, that entered into Egypt; Jacob with his free children. The first begotten is Reuben;
46.9: the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.
46.10: The sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a woman of Canaan.
46.11: The sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
46.12: The sons of Judah; Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Perez, and Zarah. Forsooth Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan; and the sons of Perez were born, Hezron, and Hamul.
46.13: The sons of Issachar; Tola, and Phuvah, and Job, and Shimron.
46.14: The sons of Zebulun; Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.
46.15: These be the sons of Leah, which she childed to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, with Dinah, her daughter; all the souls of his sons and daughters by Leah, three and thirty.
46.16: The sons of Gad; Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
46.17: The sons of Asher; Jimnah, and Ishuah, and Isui, and Beriah; and Serah, the sister of them. The sons of Beriah; Heber, and Malchiel.
46.18: These were the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and through whom Jacob begat these sixteen persons.
46.19: The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife, were Joseph and Benjamin.
46.20: And two sons were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, Manasseh and Ephraim, which Asenath, [[the]] daughter of Potipherah, priest of Heliopolis, childed to him.
46.21: The sons of Benjamin were Belah, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, and Ehi, and Rosh, and Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.
46.22: These were the sons of Rachel, the which Jacob begat through her; all the persons were fourteen.
46.24: The sons of Naphtali; Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.
46.25: These were the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter. And Jacob begat these through Bilhah; all the souls were seven.
46.26: And all the men that entered with Jacob into Egypt, and went out of his thigh, without his sons’ wives, were sixty and six.
46.27: Forsooth the sons of Joseph, that were born to him in the land of Egypt, were two men. All the souls of the house of Jacob, that entered into Egypt, were seventy.
46.28: Forsooth Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, that he should tell to him, and he meet with them in Goshen. And when Jacob had come thither,
46.29: Joseph went up in his chariot to meet his father at the same place. And he saw Jacob, and felled on his neck, and wept betwixt embraces.
46.30: And the father said to Joseph, Now I shall die joyful, for I have seen thy face, and I leave thee living.
46.31: And Joseph spake to his brethren, and to all his father’s household, I shall go up, and tell to Pharaoh, and I shall say to him, My brethren, and the household of my father, that were in the land of Canaan, be come to me,
46.32: and they be men keepers of sheep, and have busyness of flocks to be fed; they brought with them their sheep, and great beasts, and all things which they might have.
46.33: And when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say, What is your work?
46.34: ye shall answer, We be thy servants, men shepherds, from our childhood till into this present time, both we and our fathers. Soothly ye shall say these things, that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen, for Egyptians loathe all keepers of sheep.

47.1: Therefore Joseph entered, and told to Pharaoh, and said, My father and brethren, the sheep and the great beasts of them, and all things that they wield, have come from the land of Canaan; and lo! they stand in the land of Goshen.
47.2: And Joseph ordained five, the least, or meekest, men of his brethren, to come before the king,
47.3: whom he asked, What work have ye? They answered, We thy servants be keepers of sheep, both we and our fathers;
47.4: we came into thy land to be pilgrims, that is, to dwell for a time, for no grass is to the flocks of thy servants; for hunger waxeth grievous in the land of Canaan, and we ask that thou command us thy servants to be in the land of Goshen.
47.5: And so the king said to Joseph, Thy father and thy brethren have come to thee;
47.6: the land of Egypt is in thy sight; make thou them to dwell in the best place, and give thou to them the land of Goshen; that if thou knowest that witting men be in them, ordain them masters of my beasts.
47.7: After these things Joseph brought in his father to the king, and set him before the king, and he blessed the king;
47.8: and he was asked of the king, How many be the days of the years of thy life?
47.9: And he answered, The days of [[the]] pilgrimage of my life be few and evil, of an hundred and thirty years, and those [[or they]] have not come to the days of my fathers, in which they were pilgrims.
47.10: And when Jacob had blessed the king again, he went out.
47.11: Forsooth Joseph gave to his father and [[his]] brethren a possession in Egypt, in Rameses, the best soil of [[the]] earth, as Pharaoh commanded;
47.12: and he fed them, and all the household of his father, and gave meats to them all.
47.13: For bread failed in all the world, and hunger oppressed the land, mostly of Egypt and of Canaan;
47.14: of which lands Joseph gathered all the money for the selling of wheat, and brought it into the king’s treasury.
47.15: And when price failed to the buyers, all Egypt came to Joseph, and said, Give thou loaves to us; why shall we die before thee, while money faileth?
47.16: To whom he answered, Bring ye your beasts, and I shall give you meats for those [[or them]], if ye have not price.
47.17: And when they had brought those, he gave them meats for horses, and sheep, and oxen, and asses; and he sustained them in that year for the exchange of beasts.
47.18: And they came in the second year, and said to him, We cover not from our lord, that the while money faileth, also our beasts failed altogether, neither it is hid from thee, that without bodies and land, we have nothing;
47.19: why therefore shall we die, while thou seest this? both we and our land shall be thine; buy thou us into the king’s servage, and give thou us seeds to sow, lest while the tiller perisheth, the land be turned into wilderness.
47.20: Therefore Joseph bought all the land of Egypt, while all men sold him their possessions, for the greatness of hunger; and he made it and all the peoples thereof subject to Pharaoh,
47.21: from the last terms of Egypt till to the last ends thereof,
47.22: except the land of priests, that was given of the king to them, to which priests also meats were given of the common barns, and therefore they were not compelled to sell their possessions.
47.23: Therefore Joseph said to the peoples, Lo! as ye see, Pharaoh wieldeth both you and your land; now take ye seeds, and sow ye fields,
47.24: that ye may have fruits; ye shall give the fifth part to the king; I suffer to you the four residue parts into seed, and into meats, to you, and to your free children.
47.25: Which answered, Our health is in thine hands; only our God behold us, and we shall joyfully serve the king.
47.26: From that time till to this present day, in all the land of Egypt, the fifth part is paid to the kings, and it is made as into a law, without the land of priests, that was free from this condition.
47.27: Therefore Israel dwelled in Egypt, that is, in the land of Goshen, and wielded it; and he was increased, and multiplied full much.
47.28: And he lived therein sixteen [[or seventeen]] years; and all the days of his life were made an hundred and seven and forty years.
47.29: And when he saw the day of his death [[to]] nigh, he called his son Joseph to his bed, and said to him, If I have found grace in thy sight, put thine hand under mine hip, and swear that thou shalt do mercy and truth to me, that thou bury not me in Egypt;
47.30: but I shall sleep with my fathers, and take thou away me from this land, and bury me in the sepulchre of my greaters. To whom Joseph answered, I shall do that that thou commandest.
47.31: And Israel said, Therefore swear thou to me; and when Joseph swore, Israel turned to the head of the bed, and worshipped God.

48.1: And so when these things were done, it was told to Joseph, that his father was sick. And he took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and he disposed him to go.
48.2: And it was said to the eld [[or old]] man, Lo! thy son Joseph cometh to thee; which was comforted, and sat up in the bed.
48.3: And when Joseph entered to him, he said, Almighty God appeared to me in Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
48.4: and said, I shall increase thee, and multiply thee, and I shall make thee into companies of peoples, and I shall give to thee this land, and to thy seed after thee, into everlasting possession.
48.5: Therefore thy two sons, that be born to thee in the land of Egypt, before that I came hither to thee, shall be mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon, shall be areckoned to me;
48.6: forsooth the others which thou shalt beget after them shall be thine; and they shall be called by the name of their brethren in their possessions.
48.7: Forsooth when I came from Mesopotamia, Rachel was dead to me in the land of Canaan, in that way; and it was the beginning of summer; and before that I entered into Ephratah, and I buried her beside the way of Ephratah, which by another name is called Bethlehem.
48.8: Forsooth Jacob saw the sons of Joseph, and said to him, Who be these?
48.9: He answered, They be my sons, which God gave me in this place. Jacob said, Bring them to me, that I bless them.
48.10: For the eyes of Israel dimmed for great eld age, and he might not see clearly; and he kissed and embraced those children joined to him,
48.11: and he said to his son, I am not defrauded of thy sight; furthermore God hath showed to me thy seed.
48.12: And when Joseph had taken them from his father’s lap, he worshipped or honoured low to the earth.
48.13: And he set Ephraim on his right side, that is, on the left side of Israel; forsooth he set Manasseh on his left side, that is, on the right side of his father; and he joined both to him.
48.14: Which held forth the right hand, and laid it on Ephraim’s head, the younger brother; soothly he laid his left hand on Manasseh’s head, that was the more through birth. Jacob changed his hands,
48.15: and blessed his son Joseph, and said, God, in whose sight my fathers Abraham and Isaac went; God that feedeth me from my young waxing age till into this present day;
48.16: the angel that delivered me from all evils, bless these children, and my name be called on them, and the names of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac; and wax they in multitude on earth.
48.17: Forsooth Joseph saw that his father had set [[or put]] his right hand on the head of Ephraim, and he took that heavily, and he enforced or endeavoured him to raise his father’s hand, and take it from the head of Ephraim, and to bear it over upon the head of Manasseh.
48.18: And Joseph said to his father, Father, it accordeth not so; for this is the first begotten; set [[or put]] thy right hand on his head.
48.19: Which forsook to do so, and said, I know, my son, I know; and soothly this child shall be into peoples, and he shall be multiplied; but his younger brother shall be more than he, and his seed shall increase into a multitude of folks.
48.20: And he blessed them in that time, and said, Israel shall be blessed in thee, and it shall be said, God do to thee as to Ephraim and as to Manasseh. And he set Ephraim before Manasseh;
48.21: and Jacob said to Joseph, his son, Lo! I die, and God shall be with you, and shall lead you again to the land of your fathers;
48.22: I give to thee one part over thy brethren, which I took from the hand of Amorite, in my sword and bow.

49.1: Forsooth Jacob called his sons, and said to them, Be ye gathered together, that I tell what things shall come to you in the last days;
49.2: be ye gathered [[together]], and hear, ye sons of Jacob, hear ye Israel your father.
49.3: Reuben, my first begotten son, thou art my strength, and the beginning of my sorrow; thou oughtest to be the former in gifts, the more in lordship;
49.4: thou art shed [[or poured]] out as water; wax thou not, for thou ascend-edest [[or went up]] on the bed of thy father, and defouledest his bed.
49.5: Simeon and Levi, brethren, fighting vessels of wickedness;
49.6: my soul come not into the counsel of them, and my glory be not in the congregation of them; for in their strong vengeance, they killed a man, and in their [[own]] will, they under-mined the wall;
49.7: cursed be the strong vengeance of them, for it is obstinate, and the indignation of them, for it is hard; I shall part them in Jacob, and I shall scatter them in Israel.
49.8: Judah, thy brethren shall praise thee, thine hands shall be in the nolls of thine enemies; the sons of thy father shall worship thee.
49.9: Judah, the whelp of a lion; my son, thou hast gone up to the prey; thou restedest, and hast lain as a lion, and as a lioness, who shall raise him?
49.10: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Judah, and a duke of his hip, till he come that shall be sent, and he shall be the abiding of heathen men;
49.11: and he shall tie his colt at the vinery [[or vineyard]], and his she-ass at the vine; O! my son, he shall wash his stole in wine, and his mantle in the blood of the grape;
49.12: his eyes be fairer than wine, and his teeth be whiter than milk.
49.13: Zebulun shall dwell in the brink of the sea, and in the standing of ships; and he shall stretch till to Sidon.
49.14: Issachar, a strong ass, lying betwixt [[the]] terms,
49.15: saw rest, that it was good, and saw the land, that it was best, and he underset his shoulder to bear, and he was made serving to tributes.
49.16: Dan shall deem his people, as also another lineage in Israel.
49.17: Dan be made a serpent in the way, and a cerastes, that is, an horned adder, in the path, and bite he the feet of an horse, that the rider of him fall backward;
49.18: Lord, I shall abide thine health.
49.19: Gad shall be girded, and he shall fight before him, and he shall be girded behind.
49.20: Asher, his bread shall be fat, and he shall give delights to kings.
49.21: Naphtali shall be an hart sent out, and giving speeches of fairness.
49.22: Joseph, a son increasing, a son increasing, and fair in beholding; [[the]] daughters run about on the wall,
49.23: but his brethren wrathed at him, and chided him, and they had darts, and had envy to him.
49.24: His bow sat in the Strong, that is, the Lord, and the bonds of his arms and his hands were unbound by the hand of the mighty God of Jacob; of him a shepherd went out, the stone of Israel.
49.25: God of thy father shall be thine helper, and Almighty God shall bless thee, with blessings of heaven from above, and with blessings of the sea lying beneath, with blessings of teats, and of the womb;
49.26: the blessings of thy father be comforted, that is, be better than the blessings of his fathers, till the desire of everlasting hills came; blessings be made on the head of Joseph, and in the noll of Nazarite, that is, holy, among his brethren.
49.27: Benjamin, a ravishing wolf, shall eat the prey early, and in the eventide he shall part spoils.
49.28: All these were in [[the]] twelve kindreds of Israel; their father spake these things to them, and he blessed them all by proper blessings,
49.29: and he commanded to them, and said, I am soon to be gathered to my people; bury ye me with my fathers in the double den, that is in the land of Ephron the Hittite,
49.30: that is, in the den in the field at Machpelah, against Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which den Abraham bought with the field of Ephron the Hittite, into possession of a sepulchre.
49.31: There they buried him, and Sarah his wife; also Isaac was buried there, with Rebecca his wife; there also Leah lieth buried.
49.32: (This verse is omitted in the original text.)
49.33: And when the behests were ended, by which he taught his sons, he gathered together his feet on the bed, and died, and he was put to his people.

50.1: Which thing Joseph saw, and he fell on his father’s face, and wept, and kissed him;
50.2: and he commanded his servants, leeches, that they should anoint his father with sweet smelling spiceries.
50.3: While they fulfilled his behests, forty days passed, for this was the custom of dead bodies that were anointed; and Egypt bewept him seventy days.
50.4: And when the time of wailing was fulfilled, Joseph spake to the meine of Pharaoh, If I have found grace in your sight, speak ye in the ears of Pharaoh;
50.5: for my father charged me [[with an oath]], and said, Lo! I die; thou shalt bury me in my sepulchre which I digged to me in the land of Canaan; therefore I shall go up that I bury my father, and I shall turn again.
50.6: And Pharaoh said to him, Go up, and bury thy father, as thou art charged.
50.7: And when Joseph went up, all the elder men of the household of Pharaoh went with him, and all the greater men in birth of the land of Egypt;
50.8: and all the household of Joseph with their brethren, without little children, and flocks, and great beasts, which they left in the land of Goshen, went with him.
50.9: And he had chariots, and horse-men, and fellowship with him, and the company was made not little.
50.10: And they came to the cornfloor of Atad, which is set over Jordan, where they made the service of the dead body, with great wailing and strong, and filled seven days.
50.11: And when the dwellers of the land of Canaan had seen this, they said, This is a time of great wailing to the Egyptians; therefore they called the name of that place The wailing of Egypt.
50.12: Therefore the sons of Jacob did, as he had commanded to them;
50.13: and they bare him into the land of Canaan, and they buried him in the double den, which den with the field Abraham had bought of Ephron the Hittite, against the face of Mamre, into possession of a sepulchre.
50.14: And Joseph turned again into Egypt with his brethren and all the fellowship, when his father was buried.
50.15: And when their father was dead, the brethren of Joseph dreaded, and spake together, Lest peradventure he be mindful of the wrong which he suffered, and yield to us all the evil, that we did.
50.16: And they sent to him, and said, Thy father commanded to us, before that he died,
50.17: that we should say to thee these things by his words; I beseech thee, that thou forget the wickedness of thy brethren, and the sin, and [[the]] malice that they haunted against thee; also we pray thee, that thou forgive this wickedness which we did to thy father, the servant of God. When these things were heard, Joseph wept.
50.18: And his brethren came to him, and worshipped low to the earth, and said, We be thy servants.
50.19: To which he answered, Do not ye dread; whether we may against-stand God’s will?
50.20: Ye thought evil of me, and God turned it into good, that he should enhance me, as ye see in this present time, and that he should make safe many peoples;
50.21: do not ye dread, I shall feed you and your little children. And he comforted them, and spake sweetly and lightly to them;
50.22: and Joseph dwelled in Egypt, with all the house of his father. And he lived an hundred [[and ten]] years,
50.23: and he saw the sons of Ephraim till to the third generation; also the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were borne in the knees of Joseph.
50.24: When these things were done, Joseph spake to his brethren, After my death God shall visit you, and he shall make you to go up from this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
50.25: And when Joseph had charged them with an oath, and had said, God shall visit you, bear ye out with you my bones from this place;
50.26: he died, when an hundred and ten years of his life were filled; and he was anointed with sweet smelling spiceries, and he was kept in a bier in Egypt.
